Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 69, verse 1–17:

Meccan: it has one thousand and eighty-four letters, fifty-six words, and fifty-two verses.

Kamil ibn Ahmad informed us, and Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Haqqah, Allah will reckon with him with an easy reckoning." [20] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/102.]]

And Abu al-Husayn al-Khabbazi informed us, saying: Abu al-Shaykh al-Hafiz narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Uthman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Fudalah ibn Shurayk, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, who said: I heard him say: "Whoever recites eleven verses of Surah al-Haqqah will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal, and whoever recites it will have a light from above his head to his feet."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Al-Haqqah** (the Inevitable Reality). **What is al-Haqqah?** That is, the Resurrection. It was named al-Haqqah because it is certainly true (haqqat), so there is no lie in it; because in it the realities of matters and their truths become manifest; and because in it the recompense for deeds becomes due (yajibu), as one says: "haqqa 'alayhi al-shay'" when a thing becomes obligatory and is established with certainty. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But the word of punishment has become due against the disbelievers﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 71.]]. Al-Kisa'i and al-Mu'arrikh said: al-Haqqah is the Day of Truth; the Arabs say: "Haqqa li-ma 'arafta al-haqq minni" (the truth has become due to me, as you recognised the truth from me).

Al-Haqqah and al-Haqqah and al-Haqqah (al-Hiqqah) are three dialectal forms with one meaning. The first al-Haqqah is in the nominative as the subject of the inchoative, and its predicate is what follows it. It was also said: the first al-Haqqah is nominative by the second, because the second is in the position of an explanation of it, as if he were amazed by it and said: "What is the Haqqah?" just as you say: "Zayd, what is Zayd?" The second al-Haqqah is nominative by "ma," and "ma" means "what thing," and it is nominative by the second al-Haqqah. Similar to it is ﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ [[Surah al-Qari'ah: 1-2.]] and ﴿And the companions of the right hand — what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: 27.]], and similar to them.

﴿And what will make you know what the Haqqah is? Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity﴾, that is, the punishment that descended upon them when their prophet had warned them, until it fell upon them and struck their hearts. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: it means the Resurrection.

﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast﴾, that is, by their transgression and disobedience. It is a verbal noun like "al-Haqqah," and it was said: it is an adjective whose meaning is "by their overwhelming deed." This is the meaning stated by Mujahid and Ibn Zayd, and the evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿Thamud denied in their transgression﴾ [[Surah al-Shams: 11.]]. Qatadah said: it means the Overwhelming Cry that exceeded the measure of shouting, and it crushed them.

﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a violent, roaring wind﴾, which rose beyond its limits, overpowered its keepers so they could not control it, and exceeded its measure.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamdan ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Sulayman al-Bahrani narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Musa ibn al-Musayyab, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted sends no wind except by measure, and no drop of water except by measure, except on the day of 'Ad and the day of Nuh. For the water on the day of Nuh overflowed the treasuries, so they had no control over them." Then he recited: ﴿with a violent, roaring wind﴾. [21] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/61.]]

**Sakhkharaha** means: sent it and empowered it. **'Alayhim** (against them). Al-taskhir (subjugation) is the use of a thing with power.

**Sab'a layalin wa thamaniyata ayyam** (seven nights and eight days). Wahb said: these are the days that the Arabs named "the days of the old woman," a cold and violently windy period. These days were attributed to the old woman because an old woman entered a cave, and the wind followed her and killed her. The eighth day from the start of the punishment was the day the punishment ended.

It was also said: they were called the days of the old woman because they fall in the final part of winter (ajz al-shita'). They have well-known names. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf recited to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Wazir recited to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Saffar recited to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Qayyim ibn Bashshar recited to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha'lab, the poet, recited to us describing the days of the old woman:

*Kasa'a* [[al-Kasa': the severity of the cold.]] winter with seven dusty days... the days of the old woman [[al-Shahlah: the old woman.]] of the month,

So with Amir and his brother Mu'tamir... and Mu'allil and the extinguisher of embers [[al-Sihah: 3/884.]]

Winter has departed, turning back hastily, and there came to you the scorching heat of the blazing sun [[al-Najr: the heat.]]

The name of the eighth day is: Mukfi al-Za'n.

**Husuman**: Ibn 'Abbas said: in succession. Mujahid and Qatadah said: continuous, without any pause. On this view it is derived from "jasm al-kayy," which is to be repeatedly branded with the iron. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: lasting. Al-Dahhak said: complete, not abating from them until it destroyed them. 'Ata' said: ill-omened, as if it cut off good from its people. Al-Khalil said: cutting off their roots. Al-hasm means cutting and prevention, and from it comes "hasm al-da'" (cauterising the disease) and "hasm al-difa'" (blocking the defence). Yaman and al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "He cut them off (hasamahum), that is, he cut them off and destroyed them." It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), and the cutting off.

﴿So you see the people in it as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees﴾, that is, in those nights and days, ﴿prostrate﴾, dead, the plural of "sari'" (one thrown down); ﴿as if they were trunks of palm trees, hollow﴾, fallen. It was also said: hollow in their insides. ﴿Do you see any remnant of them?﴾ meaning, survival.

﴿And Pharaoh came, and those before him﴾. Abu 'Amr, al-Hasan, al-Sulami, al-Hajri, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub recited with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba' (waman qablahu? no: *wa man ma'ahu*): meaning those with him, his soldiers and followers. This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, supported by the reading of Abdullah and Ubayy: "wa man ma'ahu." Abu Musa al-Ash'ari recited: "wa man talqahu." The others recited: ﴿wa man qablahu﴾ with a fatha on the qaf and a sukun on the ba', meaning those who preceded him of the earlier generations.

﴿And the overturned cities﴾: the common reading is with the alif. Al-Hasan recited *al-mu'tafikah* without the alif. ﴿With sin﴾, that is, with error and disobedience, which is disbelief. ﴿They disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizing, overwhelming, exceeding, extraordinary.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: severe. It was also said: exceeding the punishment of the other nations.

﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾, that is, it rose beyond measure, flowing out without weight or measure. Qatadah said: the water rose fifteen cubits above everything. ﴿We carried you in the sailing ship﴾, the ark, ﴿to make it for you a reminder﴾, a lesson and admonition, ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it.﴾

Talhah recited *wa ta'iyaha* with the 'ayn sukun, imitating His saying: *wa arina*; it is transmitted differently from 'Asim and Ibn Bakr, and it is a poor, weak reading. The rest recite it with the vowel fully pronounced.

﴿An attentive ear﴾: one that understood from God what it heard.

Al-Farabi ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hayyan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Allah to make it your ear, O 'Ali." 'Ali said: "After that I never forgot anything, and it was not for me to forget." [22] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/177, no. 36526.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hasan narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Qayyim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib ibn al-Harb narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Adam narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Salih ibn Maytham narrated to us, saying: I heard Buraydah al-Aslami say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Ali: "Allah the Mighty and Majestic has commanded me to bring you near and not to push you away, to teach you, and that you should retain, and that it is a truth upon Allah the Exalted that you should retain." He said: And there was revealed: ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾. [23] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/136, no. 36426.]]

﴿Then when the Horn is blown with one blast﴾, which is the first blast. ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with one blow﴾, that is, broken and pulverised in a single crushing, becoming scattered dust. He said *fa-dukkata* (both of them) and not *dukkan* because He treated the earth as one thing and the mountains as one thing.

﴿That Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾, the Resurrection will be established. ﴿And the sky will be split, for it that Day will be frail﴾, weak. ﴿And the angels will be at its edges﴾, that is, its sides and extremities, in the dialect of Hudhayl, whose singular is *raja'* and whose dual is *rajawan*. ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: eight rows of angels, whose number none knows but Allah.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Today they are four; when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will strengthen them with four others, and they will be eight." [24] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/73.]]

Al-Imam Abu Mansur al-Hammadi informed us, saying: al-Imam Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Ja'far narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, concerning His saying: ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord﴾, who said: "Eight angels in the form of mountain goats (awwal)."

And in a hadith: "Each one of them has four faces: the face of a man, the face of a lion, the face of an ox, and the face of an eagle." [25] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/266.]]

It was also said that in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there was recited the verse of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt:

*A man and an ox beneath his right foot... and the eagle to the other, and a watchful lion.*

*The sun rises every last night, red, rising with its colour reddening;*

*It refuses, so it does not rise for us in its course except tormented, and unless it is humbled.*  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/266.]]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He has spoken truly." [26]

And it is narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: Allah the Exalted created the Throne fourth; before it He created only three things: the air, the pen, and the light. Then He created from colours of different lights: from one green light the greenness became green; from a yellow light the yellowness became yellow; from a red light the redness became red; and a white light, which is the light of lights, from which comes the light of day. Then He made it seventy thousand thousand thousand layers, none of which is without glorifying His praise and sanctifying Him with varied voices; if one of their tongues were permitted to be heard, it would destroy the mountains and palaces and make the seas sink.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The first al-Haqqah is in the nominative as the subject of the inchoative, and its predicate is what follows it. It was also said: the first al-Haqqah is nominative by the second, because the second is in the position of an explanation of it, as if he were amazed by it and said: "What is the Haqqah?" just as you say: "Zayd, what is Zayd?" The second al-Haqqah is nominative by "ma," and "ma" means "what thing," and it is nominative by the second al-Haqqah. Similar to it is ﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ [[Surah al-Qari'ah: 1-2.]] and ﴿And the companions of the right hand — what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: 27.]], and similar to them.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamdan ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Sulayman al-Bahrani narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Musa ibn al-Musayyab, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted sends no wind except by measure, and no drop of water except by measure, except on the day of 'Ad and the day of Nuh. *Kasa'a* [[al-Kasa': the severity of the cold.]] winter with seven dusty days... the days of the old woman [[al-Shahlah: the old woman.]] of the month,

So with Amir and his brother Mu'tamir... and Mu'allil and the extinguisher of embers [[al-Sihah: 3/884.]]

Winter has departed, turning back hastily, and there came to you the scorching heat of the blazing sun [[al-Najr: the heat.]]

The name of the eighth day is: Mukfi al-Za'n.

**Husuman**: Ibn 'Abbas said: in succession. Mujahid and Qatadah said: continuous, without any pause. On this view it is derived from "jasm al-kayy," which is to be repeatedly branded with the iron. Al-Khalil said: cutting off their roots. Al-hasm means cutting and prevention, and from it comes "hasm al-da'" (cauterising the disease) and "hasm al-difa'" (blocking the defence). Yaman and al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "He cut them off (hasamahum), that is, he cut them off and destroyed them." It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), and the cutting off.

﴿And the overturned cities﴾: the common reading is with the alif. Al-Hasan recited *al-mu'tafikah* without the alif. ﴿With sin﴾, that is, with error and disobedience, which is disbelief. ﴿They disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizing, overwhelming, exceeding, extraordinary.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: severe. It was also said: exceeding the punishment of the other nations.

﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾, that is, it rose beyond measure, flowing out without weight or measure. Qatadah said: the water rose fifteen cubits above everything. ﴿We carried you in the sailing ship﴾, the ark, ﴿to make it for you a reminder﴾, a lesson and admonition, ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it.﴾

He said: And there was revealed: ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾. [23] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/136, no. 36426.]]

﴿Then when the Horn is blown with one blast﴾, which is the first blast. ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with one blow﴾, that is, broken and pulverised in a single crushing, becoming scattered dust. ﴿That Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾, the Resurrection will be established. ﴿And the sky will be split, for it that Day will be frail﴾, weak. ﴿And the angels will be at its edges﴾, that is, its sides and extremities, in the dialect of Hudhayl, whose singular is *raja'* and whose dual is *rajawan*. ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: eight rows of angels, whose number none knows but Allah.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Today they are four; when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will strengthen them with four others, and they will be eight." [24] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/73.]]

Al-Imam Abu Mansur al-Hammadi informed us, saying: al-Imam Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Ja'far narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, concerning His saying: ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord﴾, who said: "Eight angels in the form of mountain goats (awwal)."

*A man and an ox beneath his right foot... and the eagle to the other, and a watchful lion.*

*It refuses, so it does not rise for us in its course except tormented, and unless it is humbled.*  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/266.]]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He has spoken truly." [26]

And it is narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: Allah the Exalted created the Throne fourth; before it He created only three things: the air, the pen, and the light. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Al-Haqqah** (the Inevitable Reality). **What is al-Haqqah?** That is, the Resurrection. It was named al-Haqqah because it is certainly true (haqqat), so there is no lie in it; because in it the realities of matters and their truths become manifest; and because in it the recompense for deeds becomes due (yajibu), as one says: "haqqa 'alayhi al-shay'" when a thing becomes obligatory and is established with certainty. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But the word of punishment has become due against the disbelievers﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 71.]]. Al-Kisa'i and al-Mu'arrikh said: al-Haqqah is the Day of Truth; the Arabs say: "Haqqa li-ma 'arafta al-haqq minni" (the truth has become due to me, as you recognised the truth from me).

Al-Haqqah and al-Haqqah and al-Haqqah (al-Hiqqah) are three dialectal forms with one meaning. The first al-Haqqah is in the nominative as the subject of the inchoative, and its predicate is what follows it. It was also said: the first al-Haqqah is nominative by the second, because the second is in the position of an explanation of it, as if he were amazed by it and said: "What is the Haqqah?" just as you say: "Zayd, what is Zayd?" The second al-Haqqah is nominative by "ma," and "ma" means "what thing," and it is nominative by the second al-Haqqah. Similar to it is ﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ [[Surah al-Qari'ah: 1-2.]] and ﴿And the companions of the right hand — what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: 27.]], and similar to them.

﴿And what will make you know what the Haqqah is? Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity﴾, that is, the punishment that descended upon them when their prophet had warned them, until it fell upon them and struck their hearts. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: it means the Resurrection.

﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast﴾, that is, by their transgression and disobedience. It is a verbal noun like "al-Haqqah," and it was said: it is an adjective whose meaning is "by their overwhelming deed." This is the meaning stated by Mujahid and Ibn Zayd, and the evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿Thamud denied in their transgression﴾ [[Surah al-Shams: 11.]]. Qatadah said: it means the Overwhelming Cry that exceeded the measure of shouting, and it crushed them.

﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a violent, roaring wind﴾, which rose beyond its limits, overpowered its keepers so they could not control it, and exceeded its measure.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamdan ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Sulayman al-Bahrani narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Musa ibn al-Musayyab, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted sends no wind except by measure, and no drop of water except by measure, except on the day of 'Ad and the day of Nuh. **Sakhkharaha** means: sent it and empowered it. **'Alayhim** (against them). Al-taskhir (subjugation) is the use of a thing with power.

**Sab'a layalin wa thamaniyata ayyam** (seven nights and eight days). Wahb said: these are the days that the Arabs named "the days of the old woman," a cold and violently windy period. These days were attributed to the old woman because an old woman entered a cave, and the wind followed her and killed her. The eighth day from the start of the punishment was the day the punishment ended.

It was also said: they were called the days of the old woman because they fall in the final part of winter (ajz al-shita'). They have well-known names. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf recited to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Wazir recited to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Saffar recited to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Qayyim ibn Bashshar recited to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha'lab, the poet, recited to us describing the days of the old woman:

*Kasa'a* [[al-Kasa': the severity of the cold.]] winter with seven dusty days... the days of the old woman [[al-Shahlah: the old woman.]] of the month,

So with Amir and his brother Mu'tamir... and Mu'allil and the extinguisher of embers [[al-Sihah: 3/884.]]

Winter has departed, turning back hastily, and there came to you the scorching heat of the blazing sun [[al-Najr: the heat.]]

The name of the eighth day is: Mukfi al-Za'n.

**Husuman**: Ibn 'Abbas said: in succession. Mujahid and Qatadah said: continuous, without any pause. On this view it is derived from "jasm al-kayy," which is to be repeatedly branded with the iron. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: lasting. Al-Dahhak said: complete, not abating from them until it destroyed them. 'Ata' said: ill-omened, as if it cut off good from its people. Al-Khalil said: cutting off their roots. Al-hasm means cutting and prevention, and from it comes "hasm al-da'" (cauterising the disease) and "hasm al-difa'" (blocking the defence). Yaman and al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "He cut them off (hasamahum), that is, he cut them off and destroyed them." It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), and the cutting off.

﴿So you see the people in it as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees﴾, that is, in those nights and days, ﴿prostrate﴾, dead, the plural of "sari'" (one thrown down); ﴿as if they were trunks of palm trees, hollow﴾, fallen. It was also said: hollow in their insides. ﴿Do you see any remnant of them?﴾ meaning, survival.

﴿And Pharaoh came, and those before him﴾. Abu 'Amr, al-Hasan, al-Sulami, al-Hajri, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub recited with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba' (waman qablahu? no: *wa man ma'ahu*): meaning those with him, his soldiers and followers. This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, supported by the reading of Abdullah and Ubayy: "wa man ma'ahu." Abu Musa al-Ash'ari recited: "wa man talqahu." The others recited: ﴿wa man qablahu﴾ with a fatha on the qaf and a sukun on the ba', meaning those who preceded him of the earlier generations.

﴿And the overturned cities﴾: the common reading is with the alif. Al-Hasan recited *al-mu'tafikah* without the alif. ﴿With sin﴾, that is, with error and disobedience, which is disbelief. ﴿They disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizing, overwhelming, exceeding, extraordinary.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: severe. It was also said: exceeding the punishment of the other nations.

﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾, that is, it rose beyond measure, flowing out without weight or measure. Qatadah said: the water rose fifteen cubits above everything. ﴿We carried you in the sailing ship﴾, the ark, ﴿to make it for you a reminder﴾, a lesson and admonition, ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it.﴾

Talhah recited *wa ta'iyaha* with the 'ayn sukun, imitating His saying: *wa arina*; it is transmitted differently from 'Asim and Ibn Bakr, and it is a poor, weak reading. The rest recite it with the vowel fully pronounced.

Al-Farabi ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hayyan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Allah to make it your ear, O 'Ali." He said: And there was revealed: ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾. [23] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/136, no. 36426.]]

﴿Then when the Horn is blown with one blast﴾, which is the first blast. ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with one blow﴾, that is, broken and pulverised in a single crushing, becoming scattered dust. He said *fa-dukkata* (both of them) and not *dukkan* because He treated the earth as one thing and the mountains as one thing.

﴿That Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾, the Resurrection will be established. ﴿And the sky will be split, for it that Day will be frail﴾, weak. ﴿And the angels will be at its edges﴾, that is, its sides and extremities, in the dialect of Hudhayl, whose singular is *raja'* and whose dual is *rajawan*. ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: eight rows of angels, whose number none knows but Allah.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Today they are four; when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will strengthen them with four others, and they will be eight." [24] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/73.]]

Al-Imam Abu Mansur al-Hammadi informed us, saying: al-Imam Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Ja'far narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, concerning His saying: ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord﴾, who said: "Eight angels in the form of mountain goats (awwal)."

*A man and an ox beneath his right foot... and the eagle to the other, and a watchful lion.*

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He has spoken truly." [26]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But the word of punishment has become due against the disbelievers﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 71.]]. Al-Kisa'i and al-Mu'arrikh said: al-Haqqah is the Day of Truth; the Arabs say: "Haqqa li-ma 'arafta al-haqq minni" (the truth has become due to me, as you recognised the truth from me).

Al-Haqqah and al-Haqqah and al-Haqqah (al-Hiqqah) are three dialectal forms with one meaning. The first al-Haqqah is in the nominative as the subject of the inchoative, and its predicate is what follows it. It was also said: the first al-Haqqah is nominative by the second, because the second is in the position of an explanation of it, as if he were amazed by it and said: "What is the Haqqah?" just as you say: "Zayd, what is Zayd?" The second al-Haqqah is nominative by "ma," and "ma" means "what thing," and it is nominative by the second al-Haqqah. Similar to it is ﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ [[Surah al-Qari'ah: 1-2.]] and ﴿And the companions of the right hand — what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: 27.]], and similar to them.

﴿And what will make you know what the Haqqah is? Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity﴾, that is, the punishment that descended upon them when their prophet had warned them, until it fell upon them and struck their hearts. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: it means the Resurrection.

﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast﴾, that is, by their transgression and disobedience. It is a verbal noun like "al-Haqqah," and it was said: it is an adjective whose meaning is "by their overwhelming deed." This is the meaning stated by Mujahid and Ibn Zayd, and the evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿Thamud denied in their transgression﴾ [[Surah al-Shams: 11.]]. Qatadah said: it means the Overwhelming Cry that exceeded the measure of shouting, and it crushed them.

﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a violent, roaring wind﴾, which rose beyond its limits, overpowered its keepers so they could not control it, and exceeded its measure.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamdan ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Sulayman al-Bahrani narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Musa ibn al-Musayyab, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted sends no wind except by measure, and no drop of water except by measure, except on the day of 'Ad and the day of Nuh. For the water on the day of Nuh overflowed the treasuries, so they had no control over them." Then he recited: ﴿with a violent, roaring wind﴾. [21] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/61.]]

**Sakhkharaha** means: sent it and empowered it. **'Alayhim** (against them). Al-taskhir (subjugation) is the use of a thing with power.

**Sab'a layalin wa thamaniyata ayyam** (seven nights and eight days). Wahb said: these are the days that the Arabs named "the days of the old woman," a cold and violently windy period. These days were attributed to the old woman because an old woman entered a cave, and the wind followed her and killed her. The eighth day from the start of the punishment was the day the punishment ended.

It was also said: they were called the days of the old woman because they fall in the final part of winter (ajz al-shita'). They have well-known names. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf recited to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Wazir recited to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Saffar recited to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Qayyim ibn Bashshar recited to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha'lab, the poet, recited to us describing the days of the old woman:

*Kasa'a* [[al-Kasa': the severity of the cold.]] winter with seven dusty days... the days of the old woman [[al-Shahlah: the old woman.]] of the month,

So with Amir and his brother Mu'tamir... and Mu'allil and the extinguisher of embers [[al-Sihah: 3/884.]]

Winter has departed, turning back hastily, and there came to you the scorching heat of the blazing sun [[al-Najr: the heat.]]

The name of the eighth day is: Mukfi al-Za'n.

**Husuman**: Ibn 'Abbas said: in succession. Mujahid and Qatadah said: continuous, without any pause. On this view it is derived from "jasm al-kayy," which is to be repeatedly branded with the iron. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: lasting. Al-Dahhak said: complete, not abating from them until it destroyed them. 'Ata' said: ill-omened, as if it cut off good from its people. Al-Khalil said: cutting off their roots. Al-hasm means cutting and prevention, and from it comes "hasm al-da'" (cauterising the disease) and "hasm al-difa'" (blocking the defence). Yaman and al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "He cut them off (hasamahum), that is, he cut them off and destroyed them." It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), and the cutting off.

﴿So you see the people in it as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees﴾, that is, in those nights and days, ﴿prostrate﴾, dead, the plural of "sari'" (one thrown down); ﴿as if they were trunks of palm trees, hollow﴾, fallen. It was also said: hollow in their insides. ﴿Do you see any remnant of them?﴾ meaning, survival.

﴿And Pharaoh came, and those before him﴾. Abu 'Amr, al-Hasan, al-Sulami, al-Hajri, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub recited with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba' (waman qablahu? no: *wa man ma'ahu*): meaning those with him, his soldiers and followers. This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, supported by the reading of Abdullah and Ubayy: "wa man ma'ahu." Abu Musa al-Ash'ari recited: "wa man talqahu." The others recited: ﴿wa man qablahu﴾ with a fatha on the qaf and a sukun on the ba', meaning those who preceded him of the earlier generations.

﴿And the overturned cities﴾: the common reading is with the alif. Al-Hasan recited *al-mu'tafikah* without the alif. ﴿With sin﴾, that is, with error and disobedience, which is disbelief. ﴿They disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizing, overwhelming, exceeding, extraordinary.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: severe. It was also said: exceeding the punishment of the other nations.

﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾, that is, it rose beyond measure, flowing out without weight or measure. Qatadah said: the water rose fifteen cubits above everything. ﴿We carried you in the sailing ship﴾, the ark, ﴿to make it for you a reminder﴾, a lesson and admonition, ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it.﴾

Talhah recited *wa ta'iyaha* with the 'ayn sukun, imitating His saying: *wa arina*; it is transmitted differently from 'Asim and Ibn Bakr, and it is a poor, weak reading. The rest recite it with the vowel fully pronounced.

﴿An attentive ear﴾: one that understood from God what it heard.

Al-Farabi ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hayyan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Allah to make it your ear, O 'Ali." 'Ali said: "After that I never forgot anything, and it was not for me to forget." [22] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/177, no. 36526.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hasan narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Qayyim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib ibn al-Harb narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Adam narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Salih ibn Maytham narrated to us, saying: I heard Buraydah al-Aslami say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Ali: "Allah the Mighty and Majestic has commanded me to bring you near and not to push you away, to teach you, and that you should retain, and that it is a truth upon Allah the Exalted that you should retain." He said: And there was revealed: ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾. [23] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/136, no. 36426.]]

﴿Then when the Horn is blown with one blast﴾, which is the first blast. ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with one blow﴾, that is, broken and pulverised in a single crushing, becoming scattered dust. He said *fa-dukkata* (both of them) and not *dukkan* because He treated the earth as one thing and the mountains as one thing.

﴿That Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾, the Resurrection will be established. ﴿And the sky will be split, for it that Day will be frail﴾, weak. ﴿And the angels will be at its edges﴾, that is, its sides and extremities, in the dialect of Hudhayl, whose singular is *raja'* and whose dual is *rajawan*. ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: eight rows of angels, whose number none knows but Allah.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Today they are four; when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will strengthen them with four others, and they will be eight." [24] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/73.]]

Al-Imam Abu Mansur al-Hammadi informed us, saying: al-Imam Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Ja'far narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, concerning His saying: ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord﴾, who said: "Eight angels in the form of mountain goats (awwal)."

And in a hadith: "Each one of them has four faces: the face of a man, the face of a lion, the face of an ox, and the face of an eagle." [25] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/266.]]

*A man and an ox beneath his right foot... and the eagle to the other, and a watchful lion.*

*The sun rises every last night, red, rising with its colour reddening;*

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He has spoken truly." [26]

And it is narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: Allah the Exalted created the Throne fourth; before it He created only three things: the air, the pen, and the light. Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamdan ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Sulayman al-Bahrani narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Musa ibn al-Musayyab, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted sends no wind except by measure, and no drop of water except by measure, except on the day of 'Ad and the day of Nuh. For the water on the day of Nuh overflowed the treasuries, so they had no control over them." Then he recited: ﴿with a violent, roaring wind﴾. [21] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/61.]]

**Sakhkharaha** means: sent it and empowered it. **'Alayhim** (against them). Al-taskhir (subjugation) is the use of a thing with power.

**Sab'a layalin wa thamaniyata ayyam** (seven nights and eight days). Wahb said: these are the days that the Arabs named "the days of the old woman," a cold and violently windy period. These days were attributed to the old woman because an old woman entered a cave, and the wind followed her and killed her. The eighth day from the start of the punishment was the day the punishment ended.

It was also said: they were called the days of the old woman because they fall in the final part of winter (ajz al-shita'). They have well-known names. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf recited to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Wazir recited to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Saffar recited to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Qayyim ibn Bashshar recited to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha'lab, the poet, recited to us describing the days of the old woman:

*Kasa'a* [[al-Kasa': the severity of the cold.]] winter with seven dusty days... the days of the old woman [[al-Shahlah: the old woman.]] of the month,

So with Amir and his brother Mu'tamir... and Mu'allil and the extinguisher of embers [[al-Sihah: 3/884.]]

Winter has departed, turning back hastily, and there came to you the scorching heat of the blazing sun [[al-Najr: the heat.]]

The name of the eighth day is: Mukfi al-Za'n.

**Husuman**: Ibn 'Abbas said: in succession. Mujahid and Qatadah said: continuous, without any pause. On this view it is derived from "jasm al-kayy," which is to be repeatedly branded with the iron. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: lasting. Al-Dahhak said: complete, not abating from them until it destroyed them. 'Ata' said: ill-omened, as if it cut off good from its people. Al-Khalil said: cutting off their roots. Al-hasm means cutting and prevention, and from it comes "hasm al-da'" (cauterising the disease) and "hasm al-difa'" (blocking the defence). Yaman and al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "He cut them off (hasamahum), that is, he cut them off and destroyed them." It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), and the cutting off.

﴿So you see the people in it as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees﴾, that is, in those nights and days, ﴿prostrate﴾, dead, the plural of "sari'" (one thrown down); ﴿as if they were trunks of palm trees, hollow﴾, fallen. It was also said: hollow in their insides. ﴿Do you see any remnant of them?﴾ meaning, survival.

﴿And Pharaoh came, and those before him﴾. Abu 'Amr, al-Hasan, al-Sulami, al-Hajri, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub recited with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba' (waman qablahu? no: *wa man ma'ahu*): meaning those with him, his soldiers and followers. This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, supported by the reading of Abdullah and Ubayy: "wa man ma'ahu." Abu Musa al-Ash'ari recited: "wa man talqahu." The others recited: ﴿wa man qablahu﴾ with a fatha on the qaf and a sukun on the ba', meaning those who preceded him of the earlier generations.

﴿And the overturned cities﴾: the common reading is with the alif. Al-Hasan recited *al-mu'tafikah* without the alif. ﴿With sin﴾, that is, with error and disobedience, which is disbelief. ﴿They disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizing, overwhelming, exceeding, extraordinary.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: severe. It was also said: exceeding the punishment of the other nations.

﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾, that is, it rose beyond measure, flowing out without weight or measure. Qatadah said: the water rose fifteen cubits above everything. ﴿We carried you in the sailing ship﴾, the ark, ﴿to make it for you a reminder﴾, a lesson and admonition, ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it.﴾

Talhah recited *wa ta'iyaha* with the 'ayn sukun, imitating His saying: *wa arina*; it is transmitted differently from 'Asim and Ibn Bakr, and it is a poor, weak reading. The rest recite it with the vowel fully pronounced.

﴿An attentive ear﴾: one that understood from God what it heard.

Al-Farabi ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hayyan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Allah to make it your ear, O 'Ali." 'Ali said: "After that I never forgot anything, and it was not for me to forget." [22] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/177, no. 36526.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hasan narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Qayyim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib ibn al-Harb narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Adam narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Salih ibn Maytham narrated to us, saying: I heard Buraydah al-Aslami say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Ali: "Allah the Mighty and Majestic has commanded me to bring you near and not to push you away, to teach you, and that you should retain, and that it is a truth upon Allah the Exalted that you should retain." He said: And there was revealed: ﴿and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾. [23] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/136, no. 36426.]]

﴿Then when the Horn is blown with one blast﴾, which is the first blast. ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with one blow﴾, that is, broken and pulverised in a single crushing, becoming scattered dust. He said *fa-dukkata* (both of them) and not *dukkan* because He treated the earth as one thing and the mountains as one thing.

﴿That Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾, the Resurrection will be established. ﴿And the sky will be split, for it that Day will be frail﴾, weak. ﴿And the angels will be at its edges﴾, that is, its sides and extremities, in the dialect of Hudhayl, whose singular is *raja'* and whose dual is *rajawan*. ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: eight rows of angels, whose number none knows but Allah.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Today they are four; when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will strengthen them with four others, and they will be eight." [24] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/73.]]

Al-Imam Abu Mansur al-Hammadi informed us, saying: al-Imam Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Ja'far narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, concerning His saying: ﴿And above them, that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord﴾, who said: "Eight angels in the form of mountain goats (awwal)."

And in a hadith: "Each one of them has four faces: the face of a man, the face of a lion, the face of an ox, and the face of an eagle." [25] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/266.]]

It was also said that in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there was recited the verse of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt:

*A man and an ox beneath his right foot... and the eagle to the other, and a watchful lion.*

*The sun rises every last night, red, rising with its colour reddening;*

*It refuses, so it does not rise for us in its course except tormented, and unless it is humbled.*  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/266.]]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He has spoken truly." [26]

And it is narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: Allah the Exalted created the Throne fourth; before it He created only three things: the air, the pen, and the light. Then He created from colours of different lights: from one green light the greenness became green; from a yellow light the yellowness became yellow; from a red light the redness became red; and a white light, which is the light of lights, from which comes the light of day. Then He made it seventy thousand thousand thousand layers, none of which is without glorifying His praise and sanctifying Him with varied voices; if one of their tongues were permitted to be heard, it would destroy the mountains and palaces and make the seas sink.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 69, verses 18–52:**

يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لا تَخْفى بالياء كوفي غير عاصم والباقون بالتاء مِنْكُمْ خافِيَةٌ

"On that Day you will be exposed; not hidden [*la takhfa*, with the yā’ read by Kūfī readers other than ʿĀṣim, and with the tā’ by the rest] from you will be any secret."

In a ḥadīth he said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the first two, they are disputes, quarrels [*ghayr mawjūda fī al-maṣdar*.] and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly into their hands, so one will take his book in his right hand and another will take it in his left." [27] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/414.]]

فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ أي تعالوا اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ ها الوقف وأخواته مثله إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ علمت وأيقنت أَنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ.

"As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: 'Here, take [*hāʾumu*, meaning come here] and read my record [*iqraʾū kitābiyah*]. Indeed, I was certain [*ẓanantu*, meaning I knew and was sure] that I would meet my reckoning.'" The pausal *hāʾ* (*ha al-waqf*) and its like are treated the same way.

Al-Ḥasan informed us, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Qayyim ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Marwazī narrated to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, saying: Marḥūm ibn Abī Arṭabān, the paternal cousin of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAwn, narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of this Ummah to be given his record in his right hand will be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he will have a radiance like the radiance of the sun!" It was said to him: "Then where is Abū Bakr?" He said: "Far, far! The angels have escorted him to Paradise!" [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/269.]]

Al-Ḥasan informed us, narrating to us Manṣūr ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Nahāwandī, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Asʿad al-Burūjirdī narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr narrated to us from Ḥammād, from Salamah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O ʿĀʾishah, all people will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except Abū Bakr." [28] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 11/558, ḥ 32635, and ḥ 32636 with variation.]]

فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ مرضية كقوله: ماءٍ دافِقٍ [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]] وقيل: ذات رضا مثل لأبن وتأمن فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ رفيعة قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ ثمارها قريبة ينالها القائم والقاعد والمضطجع، يقال لهم كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ قدّمتم لآخرتكم من الأعمال الصالحة في الأيام الماضية وهي الدنيا.

"So he will be in a pleasing life [*ʿīshatin rāḍiyah*], meaning one that is pleased, like His saying: [*māʾin dāfiq*, a gushing fluid] [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]]. It was also said: meaning one that has contentment, like *labin* and *tāmin*. In a lofty Garden [*jannatin ʿāliyah*], lofty and elevated, its fruits [*quṭūfuhā*] near at hand, meaning its fruits are close. Those who stand, sit or lie down can reach them. It will be said to them: 'Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past [*al-ayyām al-khāliyah*]', meaning the righteous deeds you sent forward for your Hereafter during the past days, which are the life of this world."

Al-Ḥusayn informed me, saying: al-Quṭayʿī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullāh narrated to us, saying: I was informed from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: I heard Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Khayfī say: "It has reached us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'O My friends, how long I have looked at you in the world, while your lips were dried of drinks, your eyes were sunken, and your bellies were emptied. So be today in your bliss, and eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past.'"

وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ قال ابن الثابت: تلوى يده اليسرى خلف ظهره ثمّ يعطى كتابه. وقيل: تنزع من صدره إلى خلف ظهره فَيَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ وَلَمْ أَدْرِ ما حِسابِيَهْ يا لَيْتَها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ يقول: يا ليت الموتة التي متّها في الدنيا كانت القاضية الفارغة من كل ما بعدها، فلم أبعث بعده، والقاضية موت الأحياء بعدها. وقيل: معناه يا ليتني متّ فاسترحت. قال قتادة: تمنّى الموت ولم يكن عنده في الدنيا شيء أكره من الموت.

"As for him who is given his record in his left hand, Ibn al-Thābit said: His left hand will be twisted behind his back, and then his record will be given to him. It was also said: it will be pulled out from his chest to behind his back. He will say: 'Would that I had not been given my record, and had not known my reckoning! Would that it had been the end [*al-qāḍiyah*]!' He means: Would that the death I died in the world had been the decisive end, with nothing after it, so that I would not have been raised after it. *Al-qāḍiyah* is the death after which there is no living. It was also said: the meaning is 'Would that I had died and been at rest.' Qatādah said: He wished for death, and there was nothing in the world more hateful to him than death."

ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ ذهبت عنّي حجّتي عن أكثر المفسّرين، وقال ابن زيد: زال عنّي ملكي وقولي فيقول الله لخزنة جهنّم: خُذُوهُ، ويروى أنّه يجتمع على شخص واحد من أهل النار مائة ألف من الزبانية، فيقطع في أيديهم قال: فلا يرى على أيديهم منه إلّا الودك، ثمّ يعاد خلقا جديدا.

"My wealth has not availed me; my authority has perished from me [*halaka ʿannī sulṭāniyah*]. According to most of the exegetes, this means my proof has gone from me. Ibn Zayd said: my kingdom and my speech have departed from me. Then Allah will say to the guardians of Hell: 'Seize him!' It is related that a hundred thousand of the Zabaniyah will gather upon one person from the people of the Fire, and they will be cut to pieces in their hands. He said: 'Nothing will be seen on their hands from him except the grease, and then he will be restored to a new creation.'"

فَغُلُّوهُ ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ أدخلوه ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ فأدخلوه في ذراع الملك، فيدخل دبره ويخرج من منخريه. وقيل: يدخل من فيه ويخرج من دبره.

"'Seize him and bind him, then burn him in the Blaze [*ṣallūhu*, meaning cast him in]. Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits [*dhirāʿan*], thread him [*fa-usluku̇hu*]', meaning they will insert him into the cubit of the king, so it enters through his anus and comes out through his nostrils. It was also said: it enters through his mouth and exits through his anus."

روى سفيان عن بسر بن دعلوق عن نوف البكالي قال: كلّ ذراع سبعون باعا والباع أبعد ممّا بينك وبين مكّة، وكان في رحبة الكوفة [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]] .

"Sufyān narrated from Bisr ibn Daʿlūq, from Nawf al-Bakālī, who said: Each cubit is seventy fathoms [*bāʿ*], and the fathom is farther than the distance between you and Makkah. It was in the courtyard [*raḥbah*] of Kufa." [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]]

وقال سفيان الثوري: كلّ ذراع من سبعين ذراعا سبعون ذراعا وقال: بأي ذراع هو؟،

"Sufyān al-Thawrī said: Each cubit of the seventy cubits is seventy cubits. And he said: 'By which cubit is it?'"

وقال عبد الله بن عمرو ابن العاص: قال رسول الله ﷺ‎: «لو أن رصاصة مثل هذه- وأشار إلى جمجمة- أرسلت من السماء إلى الأرض فهي مسيرة خمسمائة سنة بلغت الأرض قبل الليل، ولو أنّها أرسلت من رأس السلسلة لسارت أربعين خريفا الليل والنهار قبل أن تبلغ أصلها أو قعرها» [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]] .

"ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If a lead ball like this one—and he pointed to a skull—were sent down from the sky to the earth, it would take five hundred years to reach the earth, and it would arrive before nightfall. But if it were sent from the head of the chain, it would travel forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its base or its bottom.'" [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]]

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا ابن حبش قال: حدّثنا ابن زنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن عليّ قال: حدّثنا سلمة قال: حدّثنا عبد الرزاق قال: حدّثنا بكار ابن عبد الله عن ابن أبي مليكة عن عبد الله بن حنظلة عن كعب في قوله: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ قال: لو جمع حديد الدنيا ما وزن حلقة منها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Ḥabash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Bakkār ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to us from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥanẓalah, from Kaʿb, regarding His saying: 'Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him.' He said: 'If all the iron of the world were gathered, it would not weigh one link of it.'"

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن علويه قال:

حدّثنا إسماعيل بن عيسى قال: حدّثنا المسيب قال: حدّثنا سويد بن يحيى قال: بلغني أن جميع أهل النار في تلك السلسلة، ولو أن حلقة منها وضعت على جبل لذاب من حرّها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlawayh narrated to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyib narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: It has reached me that all the people of the Fire are in that chain, and if one link of it were placed on a mountain, it would melt from its heat."

إِنَّهُ كانَ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هاهُنا حَمِيمٌ صديق، وقيل: قريب يعينه، وقيل: هو مأخوذ من الحميم، وهو الماء الحار كأنه الصديق الذي يرق ويحترق قلبه له. وَلا طَعامٌ وليس له اليوم طعام. إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ وهو صديد أهل النار مأخوذ من الغسل كأنه غسالة جروحهم وقروحهم، وقال الضحاك والربيع: هو شجر يأكله أهل النار. لا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخاطِؤُنَ المذنبون وهم الكافرون.

"Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty, and did not urge the feeding of the needy. So today he has no close friend here [*ḥamīm*], meaning a friend. It was also said: a relative who would help him. It was also said: it is derived from *ḥamīm*, which is hot water, as if he were a friend whose heart softens and burns for him. And no food [*ṭaʿām*], meaning he has no food today, except from *ghislīn*, which is the pus of the people of the Fire, derived from *ghasl* (washing), as if it were the washings of their wounds and sores. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Rabīʿ said: it is a tree that the people of the Fire eat. None eat it except *al-khāṭiʾūn*, meaning the sinners, who are the disbelievers."

فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِما تُبْصِرُونَ وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ ترون وما لا ترون، وأراد جميع المكونات والموجودات، وقيل: الدنيا والآخرة. وقيل: ما في ظهر السماء والأرض وما في بطنها. وقيل:

الأجسام والأرواح.

"'So I swear by what you see and what you do not see' [*fa-lā uqsimu*]: what you see and what you do not see. He intended all created things and existing things. It was also said: this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: what is on the surface of the heaven and earth and what is in their depths. It was also said: bodies and spirits."

وقيل: النعم الظاهرة والباطنة.

"It was also said: the apparent and hidden blessings."

وقال جعفر الصادق: بِما تُبْصِرُونَ من صنعي في ملكي وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من برّي بأوليائي.

"Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: 'What you see' is of My making in My kingdom, and 'what you do not see' is of My kindness to My friends."

وقال الجنيد: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار الرسالة والوحي على حسن محمد وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من السر معه ليلة الإسراء. وقيل: ما أظهر الله للملائكة واللوح والقلم، وما استأثر بعلمه فلم يطلع عليه أحدا.

"al-Junayd said: 'What you see' is of the signs of the message and revelation upon the beauty of Muḥammad, and 'what you do not see' is of the secret with him on the night of the Isrāʾ (Night Journey). It was also said: what Allah revealed to the angels, the Preserved Tablet and the Pen, and what He kept to Himself so that no one was informed of it."

وقيل: ما تُبْصِرُونَ: الإنس وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ: الجن والملائكة. وقال ابن عطا: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار القدرة وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من أسرار القرية.

"It was also said: 'What you see' is mankind, and 'what you do not see' is the jinn and the angels. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: 'What you see' is of the traces of power, and 'what you do not see' is of the secrets of the Unseen."

إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ أي تلاوة محمد وتبليغه، وقيل: لقول مرسل رسول كريم فحذف كقوله وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]] .

"Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger [*qawlu rasūlin karīm*], meaning the recitation and conveyance of Muḥammad. It was also said: it is the word of a sent messenger, with the word omitted, like His saying: 'And ask the town' [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]]."

وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب أبو حاتم: يؤمنون ويذكرون بالياء، وغيرهم بالتاء فيهما تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ تخرّص واختلق عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ قيل: من صلة مجازه:

"'And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.' Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqūb and Abū Ḥātim read *yu'minūna* and *yadhakkarūna* with the yā’, while the others read them with the tā’ in both places. 'It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings [*taqawwala*, meaning he invented and forged], We would have seized him by the right hand.' It was said: this is a metaphor meaning:"

لعاقبناه وانتقمنا منه بالحق كقوله: قالُوا إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]] أي من قبل الحق.

"'We would have punished him and avenged Ourselves upon him with the truth,' like His saying: 'You used to come to us from the right' [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]], meaning from the side of truth."

وقال ابن عباس: لأخذناه بالقوة والقدرة، كقول الشاعر:

إذا ما راية رفعت لمجد ... تلقّاها غرابة باليمن [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

"Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'We would have seized him with strength and power,' like the poet's words:

'When a banner is raised for glory, / Gharābah receives it with the right hand.'" [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

وقيل: معناه لأخذنا منه باليد اليمنى من يديه، وهو مثل معناه لأذللناه وأهناه، وهذا كقوله: ذي السلطان إذا أراد الاستخفاف ببعض من بين يديه، واهانته لبعض أعوانه، خذ بيده فاقمه، واعتمد ابن جرير هذا التأويل.

"It was also said: the meaning is 'We would have seized him by his right hand from his hands,' and this is an image meaning 'We would have humiliated him and disgraced him.' This is like the case of a ruler who wishes to belittle someone before him, or to humiliate one of his aides: he takes his hand and makes him stand. Ibn Jarīr adopted this interpretation."

ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ نياط القلب، عن ابن عباس وأكثر الناس، وقال قتادة: حبل القلب، وقال مجاهد: الحبل الذي في الظهر. وقيل: هو عرق بين العلباء والحلقوم.

"'Then We would have cut from him the *watīn*', the heart's tendon, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and most people. Qatādah said: it is the cord of the heart. Mujāhid said: it is the cord in the back. It was also said: it is a vein between the *ʿalbāʾ* (nape) and the throat."

فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ مانعين يحجزوننا عن عقوبته وما نفعله به وإنّما جمع وهو فعل واحد ردا على معناه كقوله: لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]] ،

"'Then not one of you could withhold Us from him', meaning preventing Us from punishing him and from what We do to him. The plural *ḥājizīn* is used although the verb is singular, returning to the sense of the word *aḥad* (one), like His saying: 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers' [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]],"

وقال (عليه السلام) :

«لم تحل الغنائم لأحد [[في بعض المصادر: لقوم.]] سود الرؤوس [ممّن] قبلكم»

[30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] لفظه واحد ومعناه الجميع.

"and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Spoils were not made lawful for any black-headed one [*li-aḥad* (for anyone)] [*li-qawm* in some sources] before you [*mimman qablakum*].' [30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] Its wording is singular and its meaning is plural."

وَإِنَّهُ يعني القرآن لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ إذا رأوا ثواب متابعيه وقد خالفوه. وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ أضافه إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ الذي كلّ شيء في جنب عظمته صغير.

"'And indeed it, meaning the Qur'an, is a reminder for the God-fearing. And indeed We know that among you are deniers. And indeed it is a cause of anguish for the disbelievers' when they see the reward of its followers while they opposed it. 'And indeed it is the certain truth', which he attributed to Himself because the two wordings differ. 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty', He before whose greatness everything is small."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 69, verses 18–52:**

يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لا تَخْفى بالياء كوفي غير عاصم والباقون بالتاء مِنْكُمْ خافِيَةٌ

"On that Day you will be exposed; not hidden [*la takhfa*, with the yā’ read by Kūfī readers other than ʿĀṣim, and with the tā’ by the rest] from you will be any secret."

In a ḥadīth he said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the first two, they are disputes, quarrels [*ghayr mawjūda fī al-maṣdar*.] and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly into their hands, so one will take his book in his right hand and another will take it in his left." [27] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/414.]]

فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ أي تعالوا اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ ها الوقف وأخواته مثله إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ علمت وأيقنت أَنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ.

"As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: 'Here, take [*hāʾumu*, meaning come here] and read my record [*iqraʾū kitābiyah*]. Indeed, I was certain [*ẓanantu*, meaning I knew and was sure] that I would meet my reckoning.'" The pausal *hāʾ* (*ha al-waqf*) and its like are treated the same way.

Al-Ḥasan informed us, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Qayyim ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Marwazī narrated to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, saying: Marḥūm ibn Abī Arṭabān, the paternal cousin of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAwn, narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of this Ummah to be given his record in his right hand will be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he will have a radiance like the radiance of the sun!" It was said to him: "Then where is Abū Bakr?" He said: "Far, far! The angels have escorted him to Paradise!" [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/269.]]

Al-Ḥasan informed us, narrating to us Manṣūr ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Nahāwandī, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Asʿad al-Burūjirdī narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr narrated to us from Ḥammād, from Salamah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O ʿĀʾishah, all people will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except Abū Bakr." [28] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 11/558, ḥ 32635, and ḥ 32636 with variation.]]

فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ مرضية كقوله: ماءٍ دافِقٍ [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]] وقيل: ذات رضا مثل لأبن وتأمن فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ رفيعة قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ ثمارها قريبة ينالها القائم والقاعد والمضطجع، يقال لهم كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ قدّمتم لآخرتكم من الأعمال الصالحة في الأيام الماضية وهي الدنيا.

"So he will be in a pleasing life [*ʿīshatin rāḍiyah*], meaning one that is pleased, like His saying: [*māʾin dāfiq*, a gushing fluid] [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]]. It was also said: meaning one that has contentment, like *labin* and *tāmin*. In a lofty Garden [*jannatin ʿāliyah*], lofty and elevated, its fruits [*quṭūfuhā*] near at hand, meaning its fruits are close. Those who stand, sit or lie down can reach them. It will be said to them: 'Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past [*al-ayyām al-khāliyah*]', meaning the righteous deeds you sent forward for your Hereafter during the past days, which are the life of this world."

Al-Ḥusayn informed me, saying: al-Quṭayʿī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullāh narrated to us, saying: I was informed from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: I heard Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Khayfī say: "It has reached us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'O My friends, how long I have looked at you in the world, while your lips were dried of drinks, your eyes were sunken, and your bellies were emptied. So be today in your bliss, and eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past.'"

وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ قال ابن الثابت: تلوى يده اليسرى خلف ظهره ثمّ يعطى كتابه. وقيل: تنزع من صدره إلى خلف ظهره فَيَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ وَلَمْ أَدْرِ ما حِسابِيَهْ يا لَيْتَها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ يقول: يا ليت الموتة التي متّها في الدنيا كانت القاضية الفارغة من كل ما بعدها، فلم أبعث بعده، والقاضية موت الأحياء بعدها. وقيل: معناه يا ليتني متّ فاسترحت. قال قتادة: تمنّى الموت ولم يكن عنده في الدنيا شيء أكره من الموت.

"As for him who is given his record in his left hand, Ibn al-Thābit said: His left hand will be twisted behind his back, and then his record will be given to him. It was also said: it will be pulled out from his chest to behind his back. He will say: 'Would that I had not been given my record, and had not known my reckoning! Would that it had been the end [*al-qāḍiyah*]!' He means: Would that the death I died in the world had been the decisive end, with nothing after it, so that I would not have been raised after it. *Al-qāḍiyah* is the death after which there is no living. It was also said: the meaning is 'Would that I had died and been at rest.' Qatādah said: He wished for death, and there was nothing in the world more hateful to him than death."

ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ ذهبت عنّي حجّتي عن أكثر المفسّرين، وقال ابن زيد: زال عنّي ملكي وقولي فيقول الله لخزنة جهنّم: خُذُوهُ، ويروى أنّه يجتمع على شخص واحد من أهل النار مائة ألف من الزبانية، فيقطع في أيديهم قال: فلا يرى على أيديهم منه إلّا الودك، ثمّ يعاد خلقا جديدا.

"My wealth has not availed me; my authority has perished from me [*halaka ʿannī sulṭāniyah*]. According to most of the exegetes, this means my proof has gone from me. Ibn Zayd said: my kingdom and my speech have departed from me. Then Allah will say to the guardians of Hell: 'Seize him!' It is related that a hundred thousand of the Zabaniyah will gather upon one person from the people of the Fire, and they will be cut to pieces in their hands. He said: 'Nothing will be seen on their hands from him except the grease, and then he will be restored to a new creation.'"

فَغُلُّوهُ ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ أدخلوه ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ فأدخلوه في ذراع الملك، فيدخل دبره ويخرج من منخريه. وقيل: يدخل من فيه ويخرج من دبره.

"'Seize him and bind him, then burn him in the Blaze [*ṣallūhu*, meaning cast him in]. Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits [*dhirāʿan*], thread him [*fa-usluku̇hu*]', meaning they will insert him into the cubit of the king, so it enters through his anus and comes out through his nostrils. It was also said: it enters through his mouth and exits through his anus."

روى سفيان عن بسر بن دعلوق عن نوف البكالي قال: كلّ ذراع سبعون باعا والباع أبعد ممّا بينك وبين مكّة، وكان في رحبة الكوفة [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]] .

"Sufyān narrated from Bisr ibn Daʿlūq, from Nawf al-Bakālī, who said: Each cubit is seventy fathoms [*bāʿ*], and the fathom is farther than the distance between you and Makkah. It was in the courtyard [*raḥbah*] of Kufa." [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]]

وقال سفيان الثوري: كلّ ذراع من سبعين ذراعا سبعون ذراعا وقال: بأي ذراع هو؟،

"Sufyān al-Thawrī said: Each cubit of the seventy cubits is seventy cubits. And he said: 'By which cubit is it?'"

وقال عبد الله بن عمرو ابن العاص: قال رسول الله ﷺ‎: «لو أن رصاصة مثل هذه- وأشار إلى جمجمة- أرسلت من السماء إلى الأرض فهي مسيرة خمسمائة سنة بلغت الأرض قبل الليل، ولو أنّها أرسلت من رأس السلسلة لسارت أربعين خريفا الليل والنهار قبل أن تبلغ أصلها أو قعرها» [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]] .

"ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If a lead ball like this one—and he pointed to a skull—were sent down from the sky to the earth, it would take five hundred years to reach the earth, and it would arrive before nightfall. But if it were sent from the head of the chain, it would travel forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its base or its bottom.'" [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]]

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا ابن حبش قال: حدّثنا ابن زنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن عليّ قال: حدّثنا سلمة قال: حدّثنا عبد الرزاق قال: حدّثنا بكار ابن عبد الله عن ابن أبي مليكة عن عبد الله بن حنظلة عن كعب في قوله: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ قال: لو جمع حديد الدنيا ما وزن حلقة منها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Ḥabash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Bakkār ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to us from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥanẓalah, from Kaʿb, regarding His saying: 'Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him.' He said: 'If all the iron of the world were gathered, it would not weigh one link of it.'"

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن علويه قال:

حدّثنا إسماعيل بن عيسى قال: حدّثنا المسيب قال: حدّثنا سويد بن يحيى قال: بلغني أن جميع أهل النار في تلك السلسلة، ولو أن حلقة منها وضعت على جبل لذاب من حرّها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlawayh narrated to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyib narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: It has reached me that all the people of the Fire are in that chain, and if one link of it were placed on a mountain, it would melt from its heat."

إِنَّهُ كانَ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هاهُنا حَمِيمٌ صديق، وقيل: قريب يعينه، وقيل: هو مأخوذ من الحميم، وهو الماء الحار كأنه الصديق الذي يرق ويحترق قلبه له. وَلا طَعامٌ وليس له اليوم طعام. إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ وهو صديد أهل النار مأخوذ من الغسل كأنه غسالة جروحهم وقروحهم، وقال الضحاك والربيع: هو شجر يأكله أهل النار. لا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخاطِؤُنَ المذنبون وهم الكافرون.

"Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty, and did not urge the feeding of the needy. So today he has no close friend here [*ḥamīm*], meaning a friend. It was also said: a relative who would help him. It was also said: it is derived from *ḥamīm*, which is hot water, as if he were a friend whose heart softens and burns for him. And no food [*ṭaʿām*], meaning he has no food today, except from *ghislīn*, which is the pus of the people of the Fire, derived from *ghasl* (washing), as if it were the washings of their wounds and sores. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Rabīʿ said: it is a tree that the people of the Fire eat. None eat it except *al-khāṭiʾūn*, meaning the sinners, who are the disbelievers."

فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِما تُبْصِرُونَ وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ ترون وما لا ترون، وأراد جميع المكونات والموجودات، وقيل: الدنيا والآخرة. وقيل: ما في ظهر السماء والأرض وما في بطنها. وقيل:

الأجسام والأرواح.

"'So I swear by what you see and what you do not see' [*fa-lā uqsimu*]: what you see and what you do not see. He intended all created things and existing things. It was also said: this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: what is on the surface of the heaven and earth and what is in their depths. It was also said: bodies and spirits."

وقيل: النعم الظاهرة والباطنة.

"It was also said: the apparent and hidden blessings."

وقال جعفر الصادق: بِما تُبْصِرُونَ من صنعي في ملكي وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من برّي بأوليائي.

"Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: 'What you see' is of My making in My kingdom, and 'what you do not see' is of My kindness to My friends."

وقال الجنيد: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار الرسالة والوحي على حسن محمد وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من السر معه ليلة الإسراء. وقيل: ما أظهر الله للملائكة واللوح والقلم، وما استأثر بعلمه فلم يطلع عليه أحدا.

"al-Junayd said: 'What you see' is of the signs of the message and revelation upon the beauty of Muḥammad, and 'what you do not see' is of the secret with him on the night of the Isrāʾ (Night Journey). It was also said: what Allah revealed to the angels, the Preserved Tablet and the Pen, and what He kept to Himself so that no one was informed of it."

وقيل: ما تُبْصِرُونَ: الإنس وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ: الجن والملائكة. وقال ابن عطا: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار القدرة وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من أسرار القرية.

"It was also said: 'What you see' is mankind, and 'what you do not see' is the jinn and the angels. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: 'What you see' is of the traces of power, and 'what you do not see' is of the secrets of the Unseen."

إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ أي تلاوة محمد وتبليغه، وقيل: لقول مرسل رسول كريم فحذف كقوله وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]] .

"Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger [*qawlu rasūlin karīm*], meaning the recitation and conveyance of Muḥammad. It was also said: it is the word of a sent messenger, with the word omitted, like His saying: 'And ask the town' [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]]."

وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب أبو حاتم: يؤمنون ويذكرون بالياء، وغيرهم بالتاء فيهما تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ تخرّص واختلق عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ قيل: من صلة مجازه:

"'And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.' Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqūb and Abū Ḥātim read *yu'minūna* and *yadhakkarūna* with the yā’, while the others read them with the tā’ in both places. 'It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings [*taqawwala*, meaning he invented and forged], We would have seized him by the right hand.' It was said: this is a metaphor meaning:"

لعاقبناه وانتقمنا منه بالحق كقوله: قالُوا إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]] أي من قبل الحق.

"'We would have punished him and avenged Ourselves upon him with the truth,' like His saying: 'You used to come to us from the right' [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]], meaning from the side of truth."

وقال ابن عباس: لأخذناه بالقوة والقدرة، كقول الشاعر:

إذا ما راية رفعت لمجد ... تلقّاها غرابة باليمن [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

"Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'We would have seized him with strength and power,' like the poet's words:

'When a banner is raised for glory, / Gharābah receives it with the right hand.'" [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

وقيل: معناه لأخذنا منه باليد اليمنى من يديه، وهو مثل معناه لأذللناه وأهناه، وهذا كقوله: ذي السلطان إذا أراد الاستخفاف ببعض من بين يديه، واهانته لبعض أعوانه، خذ بيده فاقمه، واعتمد ابن جرير هذا التأويل.

"It was also said: the meaning is 'We would have seized him by his right hand from his hands,' and this is an image meaning 'We would have humiliated him and disgraced him.' This is like the case of a ruler who wishes to belittle someone before him, or to humiliate one of his aides: he takes his hand and makes him stand. Ibn Jarīr adopted this interpretation."

ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ نياط القلب، عن ابن عباس وأكثر الناس، وقال قتادة: حبل القلب، وقال مجاهد: الحبل الذي في الظهر. وقيل: هو عرق بين العلباء والحلقوم.

"'Then We would have cut from him the *watīn*', the heart's tendon, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and most people. Qatādah said: it is the cord of the heart. Mujāhid said: it is the cord in the back. It was also said: it is a vein between the *ʿalbāʾ* (nape) and the throat."

فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ مانعين يحجزوننا عن عقوبته وما نفعله به وإنّما جمع وهو فعل واحد ردا على معناه كقوله: لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]] ،

"'Then not one of you could withhold Us from him', meaning preventing Us from punishing him and from what We do to him. The plural *ḥājizīn* is used although the verb is singular, returning to the sense of the word *aḥad* (one), like His saying: 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers' [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]],"

وقال (عليه السلام) :

«لم تحل الغنائم لأحد [[في بعض المصادر: لقوم.]] سود الرؤوس [ممّن] قبلكم»

[30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] لفظه واحد ومعناه الجميع.

"and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Spoils were not made lawful for any black-headed one [*li-aḥad* (for anyone)] [*li-qawm* in some sources] before you [*mimman qablakum*].' [30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] Its wording is singular and its meaning is plural."

وَإِنَّهُ يعني القرآن لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ إذا رأوا ثواب متابعيه وقد خالفوه. وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ أضافه إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ الذي كلّ شيء في جنب عظمته صغير.

"'And indeed it, meaning the Qur'an, is a reminder for the God-fearing. And indeed We know that among you are deniers. And indeed it is a cause of anguish for the disbelievers' when they see the reward of its followers while they opposed it.
