It was also said: this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: what is on the surface of the heaven and earth and what is in their depths. It was also said: bodies and spirits."

وقيل: النعم الظاهرة والباطنة.

"It was also said: the apparent and hidden blessings."

وقال جعفر الصادق: بِما تُبْصِرُونَ من صنعي في ملكي وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من برّي بأوليائي.

"Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: 'What you see' is of My making in My kingdom, and 'what you do not see' is of My kindness to My friends."

وقال الجنيد: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار الرسالة والوحي على حسن محمد وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من السر معه ليلة الإسراء. وقيل: ما أظهر الله للملائكة واللوح والقلم، وما استأثر بعلمه فلم يطلع عليه أحدا.

"al-Junayd said: 'What you see' is of the signs of the message and revelation upon the beauty of Muḥammad, and 'what you do not see' is of the secret with him on the night of the Isrāʾ (Night Journey). It was also said: what Allah revealed to the angels, the Preserved Tablet and the Pen, and what He kept to Himself so that no one was informed of it."

وقيل: ما تُبْصِرُونَ: الإنس وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ: الجن والملائكة. وقال ابن عطا: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار القدرة وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من أسرار القرية.

"It was also said: 'What you see' is mankind, and 'what you do not see' is the jinn and the angels. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: 'What you see' is of the traces of power, and 'what you do not see' is of the secrets of the Unseen."

إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ أي تلاوة محمد وتبليغه، وقيل: لقول مرسل رسول كريم فحذف كقوله وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]] .

"Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger [*qawlu rasūlin karīm*], meaning the recitation and conveyance of Muḥammad. It was also said: it is the word of a sent messenger, with the word omitted, like His saying: 'And ask the town' [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]]."

وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب أبو حاتم: يؤمنون ويذكرون بالياء، وغيرهم بالتاء فيهما تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ تخرّص واختلق عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ قيل: من صلة مجازه:

"'And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.' Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqūb and Abū Ḥātim read *yu'minūna* and *yadhakkarūna* with the yā’, while the others read them with the tā’ in both places. 'It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings [*taqawwala*, meaning he invented and forged], We would have seized him by the right hand.' It was said: this is a metaphor meaning:"

لعاقبناه وانتقمنا منه بالحق كقوله: قالُوا إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]] أي من قبل الحق.

"'We would have punished him and avenged Ourselves upon him with the truth,' like His saying: 'You used to come to us from the right' [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]], meaning from the side of truth."

وقال ابن عباس: لأخذناه بالقوة والقدرة، كقول الشاعر:

إذا ما راية رفعت لمجد ... تلقّاها غرابة باليمن [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

"Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'We would have seized him with strength and power,' like the poet's words:

'When a banner is raised for glory, / Gharābah receives it with the right hand.'" [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

وقيل: معناه لأخذنا منه باليد اليمنى من يديه، وهو مثل معناه لأذللناه وأهناه، وهذا كقوله: ذي السلطان إذا أراد الاستخفاف ببعض من بين يديه، واهانته لبعض أعوانه، خذ بيده فاقمه، واعتمد ابن جرير هذا التأويل.

"It was also said: the meaning is 'We would have seized him by his right hand from his hands,' and this is an image meaning 'We would have humiliated him and disgraced him.' This is like the case of a ruler who wishes to belittle someone before him, or to humiliate one of his aides: he takes his hand and makes him stand. Ibn Jarīr adopted this interpretation."

ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ نياط القلب، عن ابن عباس وأكثر الناس، وقال قتادة: حبل القلب، وقال مجاهد: الحبل الذي في الظهر. وقيل: هو عرق بين العلباء والحلقوم.

"'Then We would have cut from him the *watīn*', the heart's tendon, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and most people. Qatādah said: it is the cord of the heart. Mujāhid said: it is the cord in the back. It was also said: it is a vein between the *ʿalbāʾ* (nape) and the throat."

فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ مانعين يحجزوننا عن عقوبته وما نفعله به وإنّما جمع وهو فعل واحد ردا على معناه كقوله: لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]] ،

"'Then not one of you could withhold Us from him', meaning preventing Us from punishing him and from what We do to him. The plural *ḥājizīn* is used although the verb is singular, returning to the sense of the word *aḥad* (one), like His saying: 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers' [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]],"

وقال (عليه السلام) :

«لم تحل الغنائم لأحد [[في بعض المصادر: لقوم.]] سود الرؤوس [ممّن] قبلكم»

[30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] لفظه واحد ومعناه الجميع.

"and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Spoils were not made lawful for any black-headed one [*li-aḥad* (for anyone)] [*li-qawm* in some sources] before you [*mimman qablakum*].' [30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] Its wording is singular and its meaning is plural."

وَإِنَّهُ يعني القرآن لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ إذا رأوا ثواب متابعيه وقد خالفوه. وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ أضافه إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ الذي كلّ شيء في جنب عظمته صغير.

"'And indeed it, meaning the Qur'an, is a reminder for the God-fearing. And indeed We know that among you are deniers. And indeed it is a cause of anguish for the disbelievers' when they see the reward of its followers while they opposed it. 'And indeed it is the certain truth', which he attributed to Himself because the two wordings differ. 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty', He before whose greatness everything is small."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 69, verses 18–52:**

يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لا تَخْفى بالياء كوفي غير عاصم والباقون بالتاء مِنْكُمْ خافِيَةٌ

"On that Day you will be exposed; not hidden [*la takhfa*, with the yā’ read by Kūfī readers other than ʿĀṣim, and with the tā’ by the rest] from you will be any secret."

In a ḥadīth he said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the first two, they are disputes, quarrels [*ghayr mawjūda fī al-maṣdar*.] and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly into their hands, so one will take his book in his right hand and another will take it in his left." [27] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/414.]]

فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ أي تعالوا اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ ها الوقف وأخواته مثله إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ علمت وأيقنت أَنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ.

"As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: 'Here, take [*hāʾumu*, meaning come here] and read my record [*iqraʾū kitābiyah*]. Indeed, I was certain [*ẓanantu*, meaning I knew and was sure] that I would meet my reckoning.'" The pausal *hāʾ* (*ha al-waqf*) and its like are treated the same way.

Al-Ḥasan informed us, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Qayyim ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Marwazī narrated to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, saying: Marḥūm ibn Abī Arṭabān, the paternal cousin of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAwn, narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of this Ummah to be given his record in his right hand will be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he will have a radiance like the radiance of the sun!" It was said to him: "Then where is Abū Bakr?" He said: "Far, far! The angels have escorted him to Paradise!" [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/269.]]

Al-Ḥasan informed us, narrating to us Manṣūr ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Nahāwandī, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Asʿad al-Burūjirdī narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr narrated to us from Ḥammād, from Salamah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O ʿĀʾishah, all people will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except Abū Bakr." [28] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 11/558, ḥ 32635, and ḥ 32636 with variation.]]

فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ مرضية كقوله: ماءٍ دافِقٍ [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]] وقيل: ذات رضا مثل لأبن وتأمن فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ رفيعة قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ ثمارها قريبة ينالها القائم والقاعد والمضطجع، يقال لهم كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ قدّمتم لآخرتكم من الأعمال الصالحة في الأيام الماضية وهي الدنيا.

"So he will be in a pleasing life [*ʿīshatin rāḍiyah*], meaning one that is pleased, like His saying: [*māʾin dāfiq*, a gushing fluid] [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]]. It was also said: meaning one that has contentment, like *labin* and *tāmin*. In a lofty Garden [*jannatin ʿāliyah*], lofty and elevated, its fruits [*quṭūfuhā*] near at hand, meaning its fruits are close. Those who stand, sit or lie down can reach them. It will be said to them: 'Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past [*al-ayyām al-khāliyah*]', meaning the righteous deeds you sent forward for your Hereafter during the past days, which are the life of this world."

Al-Ḥusayn informed me, saying: al-Quṭayʿī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullāh narrated to us, saying: I was informed from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: I heard Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Khayfī say: "It has reached us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'O My friends, how long I have looked at you in the world, while your lips were dried of drinks, your eyes were sunken, and your bellies were emptied. So be today in your bliss, and eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past.'"

وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ قال ابن الثابت: تلوى يده اليسرى خلف ظهره ثمّ يعطى كتابه. وقيل: تنزع من صدره إلى خلف ظهره فَيَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ وَلَمْ أَدْرِ ما حِسابِيَهْ يا لَيْتَها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ يقول: يا ليت الموتة التي متّها في الدنيا كانت القاضية الفارغة من كل ما بعدها، فلم أبعث بعده، والقاضية موت الأحياء بعدها. وقيل: معناه يا ليتني متّ فاسترحت. قال قتادة: تمنّى الموت ولم يكن عنده في الدنيا شيء أكره من الموت.

"As for him who is given his record in his left hand, Ibn al-Thābit said: His left hand will be twisted behind his back, and then his record will be given to him. It was also said: it will be pulled out from his chest to behind his back. He will say: 'Would that I had not been given my record, and had not known my reckoning! Would that it had been the end [*al-qāḍiyah*]!' He means: Would that the death I died in the world had been the decisive end, with nothing after it, so that I would not have been raised after it. *Al-qāḍiyah* is the death after which there is no living. It was also said: the meaning is 'Would that I had died and been at rest.' Qatādah said: He wished for death, and there was nothing in the world more hateful to him than death."

ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ ذهبت عنّي حجّتي عن أكثر المفسّرين، وقال ابن زيد: زال عنّي ملكي وقولي فيقول الله لخزنة جهنّم: خُذُوهُ، ويروى أنّه يجتمع على شخص واحد من أهل النار مائة ألف من الزبانية، فيقطع في أيديهم قال: فلا يرى على أيديهم منه إلّا الودك، ثمّ يعاد خلقا جديدا.

"My wealth has not availed me; my authority has perished from me [*halaka ʿannī sulṭāniyah*]. According to most of the exegetes, this means my proof has gone from me. Ibn Zayd said: my kingdom and my speech have departed from me. Then Allah will say to the guardians of Hell: 'Seize him!' It is related that a hundred thousand of the Zabaniyah will gather upon one person from the people of the Fire, and they will be cut to pieces in their hands. He said: 'Nothing will be seen on their hands from him except the grease, and then he will be restored to a new creation.'"

فَغُلُّوهُ ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ أدخلوه ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ فأدخلوه في ذراع الملك، فيدخل دبره ويخرج من منخريه. وقيل: يدخل من فيه ويخرج من دبره.

"'Seize him and bind him, then burn him in the Blaze [*ṣallūhu*, meaning cast him in]. Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits [*dhirāʿan*], thread him [*fa-usluku̇hu*]', meaning they will insert him into the cubit of the king, so it enters through his anus and comes out through his nostrils. It was also said: it enters through his mouth and exits through his anus."

روى سفيان عن بسر بن دعلوق عن نوف البكالي قال: كلّ ذراع سبعون باعا والباع أبعد ممّا بينك وبين مكّة، وكان في رحبة الكوفة [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]] .

"Sufyān narrated from Bisr ibn Daʿlūq, from Nawf al-Bakālī, who said: Each cubit is seventy fathoms [*bāʿ*], and the fathom is farther than the distance between you and Makkah. It was in the courtyard [*raḥbah*] of Kufa." [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]]

وقال سفيان الثوري: كلّ ذراع من سبعين ذراعا سبعون ذراعا وقال: بأي ذراع هو؟،

"Sufyān al-Thawrī said: Each cubit of the seventy cubits is seventy cubits. And he said: 'By which cubit is it?'"

وقال عبد الله بن عمرو ابن العاص: قال رسول الله ﷺ‎: «لو أن رصاصة مثل هذه- وأشار إلى جمجمة- أرسلت من السماء إلى الأرض فهي مسيرة خمسمائة سنة بلغت الأرض قبل الليل، ولو أنّها أرسلت من رأس السلسلة لسارت أربعين خريفا الليل والنهار قبل أن تبلغ أصلها أو قعرها» [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]] .

"ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If a lead ball like this one—and he pointed to a skull—were sent down from the sky to the earth, it would take five hundred years to reach the earth, and it would arrive before nightfall. But if it were sent from the head of the chain, it would travel forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its base or its bottom.'" [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]]

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا ابن حبش قال: حدّثنا ابن زنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن عليّ قال: حدّثنا سلمة قال: حدّثنا عبد الرزاق قال: حدّثنا بكار ابن عبد الله عن ابن أبي مليكة عن عبد الله بن حنظلة عن كعب في قوله: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ قال: لو جمع حديد الدنيا ما وزن حلقة منها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Ḥabash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Bakkār ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to us from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥanẓalah, from Kaʿb, regarding His saying: 'Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him.' He said: 'If all the iron of the world were gathered, it would not weigh one link of it.'"

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن علويه قال:

حدّثنا إسماعيل بن عيسى قال: حدّثنا المسيب قال: حدّثنا سويد بن يحيى قال: بلغني أن جميع أهل النار في تلك السلسلة، ولو أن حلقة منها وضعت على جبل لذاب من حرّها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlawayh narrated to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyib narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: It has reached me that all the people of the Fire are in that chain, and if one link of it were placed on a mountain, it would melt from its heat."

إِنَّهُ كانَ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هاهُنا حَمِيمٌ صديق، وقيل: قريب يعينه، وقيل: هو مأخوذ من الحميم، وهو الماء الحار كأنه الصديق الذي يرق ويحترق قلبه له. وَلا طَعامٌ وليس له اليوم طعام. إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ وهو صديد أهل النار مأخوذ من الغسل كأنه غسالة جروحهم وقروحهم، وقال الضحاك والربيع: هو شجر يأكله أهل النار. لا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخاطِؤُنَ المذنبون وهم الكافرون.

"Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty, and did not urge the feeding of the needy. So today he has no close friend here [*ḥamīm*], meaning a friend. It was also said: a relative who would help him. It was also said: it is derived from *ḥamīm*, which is hot water, as if he were a friend whose heart softens and burns for him. And no food [*ṭaʿām*], meaning he has no food today, except from *ghislīn*, which is the pus of the people of the Fire, derived from *ghasl* (washing), as if it were the washings of their wounds and sores. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Rabīʿ said: it is a tree that the people of the Fire eat. None eat it except *al-khāṭiʾūn*, meaning the sinners, who are the disbelievers."

فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِما تُبْصِرُونَ وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ ترون وما لا ترون، وأراد جميع المكونات والموجودات، وقيل: الدنيا والآخرة. وقيل: ما في ظهر السماء والأرض وما في بطنها. وقيل:

الأجسام والأرواح.

"'So I swear by what you see and what you do not see' [*fa-lā uqsimu*]: what you see and what you do not see. He intended all created things and existing things. It was also said: this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: what is on the surface of the heaven and earth and what is in their depths. It was also said: bodies and spirits."

وقيل: النعم الظاهرة والباطنة.

"It was also said: the apparent and hidden blessings."

وقال جعفر الصادق: بِما تُبْصِرُونَ من صنعي في ملكي وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من برّي بأوليائي.

"Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: 'What you see' is of My making in My kingdom, and 'what you do not see' is of My kindness to My friends."

وقال الجنيد: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار الرسالة والوحي على حسن محمد وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من السر معه ليلة الإسراء. وقيل: ما أظهر الله للملائكة واللوح والقلم، وما استأثر بعلمه فلم يطلع عليه أحدا.

"al-Junayd said: 'What you see' is of the signs of the message and revelation upon the beauty of Muḥammad, and 'what you do not see' is of the secret with him on the night of the Isrāʾ (Night Journey). It was also said: what Allah revealed to the angels, the Preserved Tablet and the Pen, and what He kept to Himself so that no one was informed of it."

وقيل: ما تُبْصِرُونَ: الإنس وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ: الجن والملائكة. وقال ابن عطا: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار القدرة وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من أسرار القرية.

"It was also said: 'What you see' is mankind, and 'what you do not see' is the jinn and the angels. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: 'What you see' is of the traces of power, and 'what you do not see' is of the secrets of the Unseen."

إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ أي تلاوة محمد وتبليغه، وقيل: لقول مرسل رسول كريم فحذف كقوله وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]] .

"Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger [*qawlu rasūlin karīm*], meaning the recitation and conveyance of Muḥammad. It was also said: it is the word of a sent messenger, with the word omitted, like His saying: 'And ask the town' [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]]."

وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب أبو حاتم: يؤمنون ويذكرون بالياء، وغيرهم بالتاء فيهما تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ تخرّص واختلق عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ قيل: من صلة مجازه:

"'And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.' Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqūb and Abū Ḥātim read *yu'minūna* and *yadhakkarūna* with the yā’, while the others read them with the tā’ in both places. 'It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings [*taqawwala*, meaning he invented and forged], We would have seized him by the right hand.' It was said: this is a metaphor meaning:"

لعاقبناه وانتقمنا منه بالحق كقوله: قالُوا إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]] أي من قبل الحق.

"'We would have punished him and avenged Ourselves upon him with the truth,' like His saying: 'You used to come to us from the right' [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]], meaning from the side of truth."

وقال ابن عباس: لأخذناه بالقوة والقدرة، كقول الشاعر:

إذا ما راية رفعت لمجد ... تلقّاها غرابة باليمن [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

"Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'We would have seized him with strength and power,' like the poet's words:

'When a banner is raised for glory, / Gharābah receives it with the right hand.'" [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

وقيل: معناه لأخذنا منه باليد اليمنى من يديه، وهو مثل معناه لأذللناه وأهناه، وهذا كقوله: ذي السلطان إذا أراد الاستخفاف ببعض من بين يديه، واهانته لبعض أعوانه، خذ بيده فاقمه، واعتمد ابن جرير هذا التأويل.

"It was also said: the meaning is 'We would have seized him by his right hand from his hands,' and this is an image meaning 'We would have humiliated him and disgraced him.' This is like the case of a ruler who wishes to belittle someone before him, or to humiliate one of his aides: he takes his hand and makes him stand. Ibn Jarīr adopted this interpretation."

ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ نياط القلب، عن ابن عباس وأكثر الناس، وقال قتادة: حبل القلب، وقال مجاهد: الحبل الذي في الظهر. وقيل: هو عرق بين العلباء والحلقوم.

"'Then We would have cut from him the *watīn*', the heart's tendon, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and most people. Qatādah said: it is the cord of the heart. Mujāhid said: it is the cord in the back. It was also said: it is a vein between the *ʿalbāʾ* (nape) and the throat."

فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ مانعين يحجزوننا عن عقوبته وما نفعله به وإنّما جمع وهو فعل واحد ردا على معناه كقوله: لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]] ،

"'Then not one of you could withhold Us from him', meaning preventing Us from punishing him and from what We do to him. The plural *ḥājizīn* is used although the verb is singular, returning to the sense of the word *aḥad* (one), like His saying: 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers' [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]],"

وقال (عليه السلام) :

«لم تحل الغنائم لأحد [[في بعض المصادر: لقوم.]] سود الرؤوس [ممّن] قبلكم»

[30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] لفظه واحد ومعناه الجميع.

"and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Spoils were not made lawful for any black-headed one [*li-aḥad* (for anyone)] [*li-qawm* in some sources] before you [*mimman qablakum*].' [30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] Its wording is singular and its meaning is plural."

وَإِنَّهُ يعني القرآن لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ إذا رأوا ثواب متابعيه وقد خالفوه. وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ أضافه إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ الذي كلّ شيء في جنب عظمته صغير.

"'And indeed it, meaning the Qur'an, is a reminder for the God-fearing. And indeed We know that among you are deniers. And indeed it is a cause of anguish for the disbelievers' when they see the reward of its followers while they opposed it. 'And indeed it is the certain truth', which he attributed to Himself because the two wordings differ. 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty', He before whose greatness everything is small."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 69, verses 18–52:**

يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لا تَخْفى بالياء كوفي غير عاصم والباقون بالتاء مِنْكُمْ خافِيَةٌ

"On that Day you will be exposed; not hidden [*la takhfa*, with the yā’ read by Kūfī readers other than ʿĀṣim, and with the tā’ by the rest] from you will be any secret."

In a ḥadīth he said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the first two, they are disputes, quarrels [*ghayr mawjūda fī al-maṣdar*.] and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly into their hands, so one will take his book in his right hand and another will take it in his left." [27] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/414.]]

فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ أي تعالوا اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ ها الوقف وأخواته مثله إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ علمت وأيقنت أَنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ.

"As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: 'Here, take [*hāʾumu*, meaning come here] and read my record [*iqraʾū kitābiyah*]. Indeed, I was certain [*ẓanantu*, meaning I knew and was sure] that I would meet my reckoning.'" The pausal *hāʾ* (*ha al-waqf*) and its like are treated the same way.

Al-Ḥasan informed us, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Qayyim ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Marwazī narrated to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, saying: Marḥūm ibn Abī Arṭabān, the paternal cousin of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAwn, narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of this Ummah to be given his record in his right hand will be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he will have a radiance like the radiance of the sun!" It was said to him: "Then where is Abū Bakr?" He said: "Far, far! The angels have escorted him to Paradise!" [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/269.]]

Al-Ḥasan informed us, narrating to us Manṣūr ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Nahāwandī, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Asʿad al-Burūjirdī narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr narrated to us from Ḥammād, from Salamah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O ʿĀʾishah, all people will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except Abū Bakr." [28] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 11/558, ḥ 32635, and ḥ 32636 with variation.]]

فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ مرضية كقوله: ماءٍ دافِقٍ [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]] وقيل: ذات رضا مثل لأبن وتأمن فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ رفيعة قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ ثمارها قريبة ينالها القائم والقاعد والمضطجع، يقال لهم كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ قدّمتم لآخرتكم من الأعمال الصالحة في الأيام الماضية وهي الدنيا.

"So he will be in a pleasing life [*ʿīshatin rāḍiyah*], meaning one that is pleased, like His saying: [*māʾin dāfiq*, a gushing fluid] [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]]. It was also said: meaning one that has contentment, like *labin* and *tāmin*. In a lofty Garden [*jannatin ʿāliyah*], lofty and elevated, its fruits [*quṭūfuhā*] near at hand, meaning its fruits are close. Those who stand, sit or lie down can reach them. It will be said to them: 'Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past [*al-ayyām al-khāliyah*]', meaning the righteous deeds you sent forward for your Hereafter during the past days, which are the life of this world."

Al-Ḥusayn informed me, saying: al-Quṭayʿī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullāh narrated to us, saying: I was informed from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: I heard Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Khayfī say: "It has reached us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'O My friends, how long I have looked at you in the world, while your lips were dried of drinks, your eyes were sunken, and your bellies were emptied. So be today in your bliss, and eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past.'"

وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ قال ابن الثابت: تلوى يده اليسرى خلف ظهره ثمّ يعطى كتابه. وقيل: تنزع من صدره إلى خلف ظهره فَيَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ وَلَمْ أَدْرِ ما حِسابِيَهْ يا لَيْتَها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ يقول: يا ليت الموتة التي متّها في الدنيا كانت القاضية الفارغة من كل ما بعدها، فلم أبعث بعده، والقاضية موت الأحياء بعدها. وقيل: معناه يا ليتني متّ فاسترحت. قال قتادة: تمنّى الموت ولم يكن عنده في الدنيا شيء أكره من الموت.

"As for him who is given his record in his left hand, Ibn al-Thābit said: His left hand will be twisted behind his back, and then his record will be given to him. It was also said: it will be pulled out from his chest to behind his back. He will say: 'Would that I had not been given my record, and had not known my reckoning! Would that it had been the end [*al-qāḍiyah*]!' He means: Would that the death I died in the world had been the decisive end, with nothing after it, so that I would not have been raised after it. *Al-qāḍiyah* is the death after which there is no living. It was also said: the meaning is 'Would that I had died and been at rest.' Qatādah said: He wished for death, and there was nothing in the world more hateful to him than death."

ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ ذهبت عنّي حجّتي عن أكثر المفسّرين، وقال ابن زيد: زال عنّي ملكي وقولي فيقول الله لخزنة جهنّم: خُذُوهُ، ويروى أنّه يجتمع على شخص واحد من أهل النار مائة ألف من الزبانية، فيقطع في أيديهم قال: فلا يرى على أيديهم منه إلّا الودك، ثمّ يعاد خلقا جديدا.

"My wealth has not availed me; my authority has perished from me [*halaka ʿannī sulṭāniyah*]. According to most of the exegetes, this means my proof has gone from me. Ibn Zayd said: my kingdom and my speech have departed from me. Then Allah will say to the guardians of Hell: 'Seize him!' It is related that a hundred thousand of the Zabaniyah will gather upon one person from the people of the Fire, and they will be cut to pieces in their hands. He said: 'Nothing will be seen on their hands from him except the grease, and then he will be restored to a new creation.'"

فَغُلُّوهُ ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ أدخلوه ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ فأدخلوه في ذراع الملك، فيدخل دبره ويخرج من منخريه. وقيل: يدخل من فيه ويخرج من دبره.

"'Seize him and bind him, then burn him in the Blaze [*ṣallūhu*, meaning cast him in]. Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits [*dhirāʿan*], thread him [*fa-usluku̇hu*]', meaning they will insert him into the cubit of the king, so it enters through his anus and comes out through his nostrils. It was also said: it enters through his mouth and exits through his anus."

روى سفيان عن بسر بن دعلوق عن نوف البكالي قال: كلّ ذراع سبعون باعا والباع أبعد ممّا بينك وبين مكّة، وكان في رحبة الكوفة [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]] .

"Sufyān narrated from Bisr ibn Daʿlūq, from Nawf al-Bakālī, who said: Each cubit is seventy fathoms [*bāʿ*], and the fathom is farther than the distance between you and Makkah. It was in the courtyard [*raḥbah*] of Kufa." [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]]

وقال سفيان الثوري: كلّ ذراع من سبعين ذراعا سبعون ذراعا وقال: بأي ذراع هو؟،

"Sufyān al-Thawrī said: Each cubit of the seventy cubits is seventy cubits. And he said: 'By which cubit is it?'"

وقال عبد الله بن عمرو ابن العاص: قال رسول الله ﷺ‎: «لو أن رصاصة مثل هذه- وأشار إلى جمجمة- أرسلت من السماء إلى الأرض فهي مسيرة خمسمائة سنة بلغت الأرض قبل الليل، ولو أنّها أرسلت من رأس السلسلة لسارت أربعين خريفا الليل والنهار قبل أن تبلغ أصلها أو قعرها» [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]] .

"ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If a lead ball like this one—and he pointed to a skull—were sent down from the sky to the earth, it would take five hundred years to reach the earth, and it would arrive before nightfall. But if it were sent from the head of the chain, it would travel forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its base or its bottom.'" [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]]

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا ابن حبش قال: حدّثنا ابن زنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن عليّ قال: حدّثنا سلمة قال: حدّثنا عبد الرزاق قال: حدّثنا بكار ابن عبد الله عن ابن أبي مليكة عن عبد الله بن حنظلة عن كعب في قوله: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ قال: لو جمع حديد الدنيا ما وزن حلقة منها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Ḥabash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Bakkār ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to us from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥanẓalah, from Kaʿb, regarding His saying: 'Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him.' He said: 'If all the iron of the world were gathered, it would not weigh one link of it.'"

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن علويه قال:

حدّثنا إسماعيل بن عيسى قال: حدّثنا المسيب قال: حدّثنا سويد بن يحيى قال: بلغني أن جميع أهل النار في تلك السلسلة، ولو أن حلقة منها وضعت على جبل لذاب من حرّها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlawayh narrated to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyib narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: It has reached me that all the people of the Fire are in that chain, and if one link of it were placed on a mountain, it would melt from its heat."

إِنَّهُ كانَ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هاهُنا حَمِيمٌ صديق، وقيل: قريب يعينه، وقيل: هو مأخوذ من الحميم، وهو الماء الحار كأنه الصديق الذي يرق ويحترق قلبه له. وَلا طَعامٌ وليس له اليوم طعام. إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ وهو صديد أهل النار مأخوذ من الغسل كأنه غسالة جروحهم وقروحهم، وقال الضحاك والربيع: هو شجر يأكله أهل النار. لا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخاطِؤُنَ المذنبون وهم الكافرون.

"Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty, and did not urge the feeding of the needy. So today he has no close friend here [*ḥamīm*], meaning a friend. It was also said: a relative who would help him. It was also said: it is derived from *ḥamīm*, which is hot water, as if he were a friend whose heart softens and burns for him. And no food [*ṭaʿām*], meaning he has no food today, except from *ghislīn*, which is the pus of the people of the Fire, derived from *ghasl* (washing), as if it were the washings of their wounds and sores. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Rabīʿ said: it is a tree that the people of the Fire eat. None eat it except *al-khāṭiʾūn*, meaning the sinners, who are the disbelievers."

فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِما تُبْصِرُونَ وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ ترون وما لا ترون، وأراد جميع المكونات والموجودات، وقيل: الدنيا والآخرة. وقيل: ما في ظهر السماء والأرض وما في بطنها. وقيل:

الأجسام والأرواح.

"'So I swear by what you see and what you do not see' [*fa-lā uqsimu*]: what you see and what you do not see. He intended all created things and existing things. It was also said: this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: what is on the surface of the heaven and earth and what is in their depths. It was also said: bodies and spirits."

وقيل: النعم الظاهرة والباطنة.

"It was also said: the apparent and hidden blessings."

وقال جعفر الصادق: بِما تُبْصِرُونَ من صنعي في ملكي وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من برّي بأوليائي.

"Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: 'What you see' is of My making in My kingdom, and 'what you do not see' is of My kindness to My friends."

وقال الجنيد: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار الرسالة والوحي على حسن محمد وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من السر معه ليلة الإسراء. وقيل: ما أظهر الله للملائكة واللوح والقلم، وما استأثر بعلمه فلم يطلع عليه أحدا.

"al-Junayd said: 'What you see' is of the signs of the message and revelation upon the beauty of Muḥammad, and 'what you do not see' is of the secret with him on the night of the Isrāʾ (Night Journey). It was also said: what Allah revealed to the angels, the Preserved Tablet and the Pen, and what He kept to Himself so that no one was informed of it."

وقيل: ما تُبْصِرُونَ: الإنس وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ: الجن والملائكة. وقال ابن عطا: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار القدرة وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من أسرار القرية.

"It was also said: 'What you see' is mankind, and 'what you do not see' is the jinn and the angels. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: 'What you see' is of the traces of power, and 'what you do not see' is of the secrets of the Unseen."

إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ أي تلاوة محمد وتبليغه، وقيل: لقول مرسل رسول كريم فحذف كقوله وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]] .

"Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger [*qawlu rasūlin karīm*], meaning the recitation and conveyance of Muḥammad. It was also said: it is the word of a sent messenger, with the word omitted, like His saying: 'And ask the town' [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]]."

وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب أبو حاتم: يؤمنون ويذكرون بالياء، وغيرهم بالتاء فيهما تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ تخرّص واختلق عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ قيل: من صلة مجازه:

"'And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.' Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqūb and Abū Ḥātim read *yu'minūna* and *yadhakkarūna* with the yā’, while the others read them with the tā’ in both places. 'It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings [*taqawwala*, meaning he invented and forged], We would have seized him by the right hand.' It was said: this is a metaphor meaning:"

لعاقبناه وانتقمنا منه بالحق كقوله: قالُوا إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]] أي من قبل الحق.

"'We would have punished him and avenged Ourselves upon him with the truth,' like His saying: 'You used to come to us from the right' [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]], meaning from the side of truth."

وقال ابن عباس: لأخذناه بالقوة والقدرة، كقول الشاعر:

إذا ما راية رفعت لمجد ... تلقّاها غرابة باليمن [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

"Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'We would have seized him with strength and power,' like the poet's words:

'When a banner is raised for glory, / Gharābah receives it with the right hand.'" [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

وقيل: معناه لأخذنا منه باليد اليمنى من يديه، وهو مثل معناه لأذللناه وأهناه، وهذا كقوله: ذي السلطان إذا أراد الاستخفاف ببعض من بين يديه، واهانته لبعض أعوانه، خذ بيده فاقمه، واعتمد ابن جرير هذا التأويل.

"It was also said: the meaning is 'We would have seized him by his right hand from his hands,' and this is an image meaning 'We would have humiliated him and disgraced him.' This is like the case of a ruler who wishes to belittle someone before him, or to humiliate one of his aides: he takes his hand and makes him stand. Ibn Jarīr adopted this interpretation."

ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ نياط القلب، عن ابن عباس وأكثر الناس، وقال قتادة: حبل القلب، وقال مجاهد: الحبل الذي في الظهر. وقيل: هو عرق بين العلباء والحلقوم.

"'Then We would have cut from him the *watīn*', the heart's tendon, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and most people. Qatādah said: it is the cord of the heart. Mujāhid said: it is the cord in the back. It was also said: it is a vein between the *ʿalbāʾ* (nape) and the throat."

فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ مانعين يحجزوننا عن عقوبته وما نفعله به وإنّما جمع وهو فعل واحد ردا على معناه كقوله: لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]] ،

"'Then not one of you could withhold Us from him', meaning preventing Us from punishing him and from what We do to him. The plural *ḥājizīn* is used although the verb is singular, returning to the sense of the word *aḥad* (one), like His saying: 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers' [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]],"

وقال (عليه السلام) :

«لم تحل الغنائم لأحد [[في بعض المصادر: لقوم.]] سود الرؤوس [ممّن] قبلكم»

[30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] لفظه واحد ومعناه الجميع.

"and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Spoils were not made lawful for any black-headed one [*li-aḥad* (for anyone)] [*li-qawm* in some sources] before you [*mimman qablakum*].' [30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] Its wording is singular and its meaning is plural."

وَإِنَّهُ يعني القرآن لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ إذا رأوا ثواب متابعيه وقد خالفوه. وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ أضافه إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ الذي كلّ شيء في جنب عظمته صغير.

"'And indeed it, meaning the Qur'an, is a reminder for the God-fearing. And indeed We know that among you are deniers. And indeed it is a cause of anguish for the disbelievers' when they see the reward of its followers while they opposed it. 'And indeed it is the certain truth', which he attributed to Himself because the two wordings differ. 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty', He before whose greatness everything is small."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 69, verses 18–52:**

يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لا تَخْفى بالياء كوفي غير عاصم والباقون بالتاء مِنْكُمْ خافِيَةٌ

"On that Day you will be exposed; not hidden [*la takhfa*, with the yā’ read by Kūfī readers other than ʿĀṣim, and with the tā’ by the rest] from you will be any secret."

In a ḥadīth he said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the first two, they are disputes, quarrels [*ghayr mawjūda fī al-maṣdar*.] and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly into their hands, so one will take his book in his right hand and another will take it in his left." [27] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/414.]]

فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ أي تعالوا اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ ها الوقف وأخواته مثله إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ علمت وأيقنت أَنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ.

"As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: 'Here, take [*hāʾumu*, meaning come here] and read my record [*iqraʾū kitābiyah*]. Indeed, I was certain [*ẓanantu*, meaning I knew and was sure] that I would meet my reckoning.'" The pausal *hāʾ* (*ha al-waqf*) and its like are treated the same way.

Al-Ḥasan informed us, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Qayyim ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Marwazī narrated to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, saying: Marḥūm ibn Abī Arṭabān, the paternal cousin of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAwn, narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of this Ummah to be given his record in his right hand will be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he will have a radiance like the radiance of the sun!" It was said to him: "Then where is Abū Bakr?" He said: "Far, far! The angels have escorted him to Paradise!" [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/269.]]

Al-Ḥasan informed us, narrating to us Manṣūr ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Nahāwandī, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Asʿad al-Burūjirdī narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr narrated to us from Ḥammād, from Salamah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O ʿĀʾishah, all people will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except Abū Bakr." [28] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 11/558, ḥ 32635, and ḥ 32636 with variation.]]

فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ مرضية كقوله: ماءٍ دافِقٍ [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]] وقيل: ذات رضا مثل لأبن وتأمن فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ رفيعة قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ ثمارها قريبة ينالها القائم والقاعد والمضطجع، يقال لهم كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ قدّمتم لآخرتكم من الأعمال الصالحة في الأيام الماضية وهي الدنيا.

"So he will be in a pleasing life [*ʿīshatin rāḍiyah*], meaning one that is pleased, like His saying: [*māʾin dāfiq*, a gushing fluid] [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]]. It was also said: meaning one that has contentment, like *labin* and *tāmin*. In a lofty Garden [*jannatin ʿāliyah*], lofty and elevated, its fruits [*quṭūfuhā*] near at hand, meaning its fruits are close. Those who stand, sit or lie down can reach them. It will be said to them: 'Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past [*al-ayyām al-khāliyah*]', meaning the righteous deeds you sent forward for your Hereafter during the past days, which are the life of this world."

Al-Ḥusayn informed me, saying: al-Quṭayʿī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullāh narrated to us, saying: I was informed from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: I heard Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Khayfī say: "It has reached us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'O My friends, how long I have looked at you in the world, while your lips were dried of drinks, your eyes were sunken, and your bellies were emptied. So be today in your bliss, and eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past.'"

وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ قال ابن الثابت: تلوى يده اليسرى خلف ظهره ثمّ يعطى كتابه. وقيل: تنزع من صدره إلى خلف ظهره فَيَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ وَلَمْ أَدْرِ ما حِسابِيَهْ يا لَيْتَها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ يقول: يا ليت الموتة التي متّها في الدنيا كانت القاضية الفارغة من كل ما بعدها، فلم أبعث بعده، والقاضية موت الأحياء بعدها. وقيل: معناه يا ليتني متّ فاسترحت. قال قتادة: تمنّى الموت ولم يكن عنده في الدنيا شيء أكره من الموت.

"As for him who is given his record in his left hand, Ibn al-Thābit said: His left hand will be twisted behind his back, and then his record will be given to him. It was also said: it will be pulled out from his chest to behind his back. He will say: 'Would that I had not been given my record, and had not known my reckoning! Would that it had been the end [*al-qāḍiyah*]!' He means: Would that the death I died in the world had been the decisive end, with nothing after it, so that I would not have been raised after it. *Al-qāḍiyah* is the death after which there is no living. It was also said: the meaning is 'Would that I had died and been at rest.' Qatādah said: He wished for death, and there was nothing in the world more hateful to him than death."

ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ ذهبت عنّي حجّتي عن أكثر المفسّرين، وقال ابن زيد: زال عنّي ملكي وقولي فيقول الله لخزنة جهنّم: خُذُوهُ، ويروى أنّه يجتمع على شخص واحد من أهل النار مائة ألف من الزبانية، فيقطع في أيديهم قال: فلا يرى على أيديهم منه إلّا الودك، ثمّ يعاد خلقا جديدا.

"My wealth has not availed me; my authority has perished from me [*halaka ʿannī sulṭāniyah*]. According to most of the exegetes, this means my proof has gone from me. Ibn Zayd said: my kingdom and my speech have departed from me. Then Allah will say to the guardians of Hell: 'Seize him!' It is related that a hundred thousand of the Zabaniyah will gather upon one person from the people of the Fire, and they will be cut to pieces in their hands. He said: 'Nothing will be seen on their hands from him except the grease, and then he will be restored to a new creation.'"

فَغُلُّوهُ ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ أدخلوه ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ فأدخلوه في ذراع الملك، فيدخل دبره ويخرج من منخريه. وقيل: يدخل من فيه ويخرج من دبره.

"'Seize him and bind him, then burn him in the Blaze [*ṣallūhu*, meaning cast him in]. Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits [*dhirāʿan*], thread him [*fa-usluku̇hu*]', meaning they will insert him into the cubit of the king, so it enters through his anus and comes out through his nostrils. It was also said: it enters through his mouth and exits through his anus."

روى سفيان عن بسر بن دعلوق عن نوف البكالي قال: كلّ ذراع سبعون باعا والباع أبعد ممّا بينك وبين مكّة، وكان في رحبة الكوفة [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]] .

"Sufyān narrated from Bisr ibn Daʿlūq, from Nawf al-Bakālī, who said: Each cubit is seventy fathoms [*bāʿ*], and the fathom is farther than the distance between you and Makkah. It was in the courtyard [*raḥbah*] of Kufa." [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]]

وقال سفيان الثوري: كلّ ذراع من سبعين ذراعا سبعون ذراعا وقال: بأي ذراع هو؟،

"Sufyān al-Thawrī said: Each cubit of the seventy cubits is seventy cubits. And he said: 'By which cubit is it?'"

وقال عبد الله بن عمرو ابن العاص: قال رسول الله ﷺ‎: «لو أن رصاصة مثل هذه- وأشار إلى جمجمة- أرسلت من السماء إلى الأرض فهي مسيرة خمسمائة سنة بلغت الأرض قبل الليل، ولو أنّها أرسلت من رأس السلسلة لسارت أربعين خريفا الليل والنهار قبل أن تبلغ أصلها أو قعرها» [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]] .

"ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If a lead ball like this one—and he pointed to a skull—were sent down from the sky to the earth, it would take five hundred years to reach the earth, and it would arrive before nightfall. But if it were sent from the head of the chain, it would travel forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its base or its bottom.'" [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]]

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا ابن حبش قال: حدّثنا ابن زنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن عليّ قال: حدّثنا سلمة قال: حدّثنا عبد الرزاق قال: حدّثنا بكار ابن عبد الله عن ابن أبي مليكة عن عبد الله بن حنظلة عن كعب في قوله: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ قال: لو جمع حديد الدنيا ما وزن حلقة منها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Ḥabash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Bakkār ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to us from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥanẓalah, from Kaʿb, regarding His saying: 'Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him.' He said: 'If all the iron of the world were gathered, it would not weigh one link of it.'"

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن علويه قال:

حدّثنا إسماعيل بن عيسى قال: حدّثنا المسيب قال: حدّثنا سويد بن يحيى قال: بلغني أن جميع أهل النار في تلك السلسلة، ولو أن حلقة منها وضعت على جبل لذاب من حرّها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlawayh narrated to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyib narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: It has reached me that all the people of the Fire are in that chain, and if one link of it were placed on a mountain, it would melt from its heat."

إِنَّهُ كانَ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هاهُنا حَمِيمٌ صديق، وقيل: قريب يعينه، وقيل: هو مأخوذ من الحميم، وهو الماء الحار كأنه الصديق الذي يرق ويحترق قلبه له. وَلا طَعامٌ وليس له اليوم طعام. إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ وهو صديد أهل النار مأخوذ من الغسل كأنه غسالة جروحهم وقروحهم، وقال الضحاك والربيع: هو شجر يأكله أهل النار. لا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخاطِؤُنَ المذنبون وهم الكافرون.

"Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty, and did not urge the feeding of the needy. So today he has no close friend here [*ḥamīm*], meaning a friend. It was also said: a relative who would help him. It was also said: it is derived from *ḥamīm*, which is hot water, as if he were a friend whose heart softens and burns for him. And no food [*ṭaʿām*], meaning he has no food today, except from *ghislīn*, which is the pus of the people of the Fire, derived from *ghasl* (washing), as if it were the washings of their wounds and sores. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Rabīʿ said: it is a tree that the people of the Fire eat. None eat it except *al-khāṭiʾūn*, meaning the sinners, who are the disbelievers."

فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِما تُبْصِرُونَ وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ ترون وما لا ترون، وأراد جميع المكونات والموجودات، وقيل: الدنيا والآخرة. وقيل: ما في ظهر السماء والأرض وما في بطنها. وقيل:

الأجسام والأرواح.

"'So I swear by what you see and what you do not see' [*fa-lā uqsimu*]: what you see and what you do not see. He intended all created things and existing things. It was also said: this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: what is on the surface of the heaven and earth and what is in their depths. It was also said: bodies and spirits."

وقيل: النعم الظاهرة والباطنة.

"It was also said: the apparent and hidden blessings."

وقال جعفر الصادق: بِما تُبْصِرُونَ من صنعي في ملكي وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من برّي بأوليائي.

"Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: 'What you see' is of My making in My kingdom, and 'what you do not see' is of My kindness to My friends."

وقال الجنيد: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار الرسالة والوحي على حسن محمد وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من السر معه ليلة الإسراء. وقيل: ما أظهر الله للملائكة واللوح والقلم، وما استأثر بعلمه فلم يطلع عليه أحدا.

"al-Junayd said: 'What you see' is of the signs of the message and revelation upon the beauty of Muḥammad, and 'what you do not see' is of the secret with him on the night of the Isrāʾ (Night Journey). It was also said: what Allah revealed to the angels, the Preserved Tablet and the Pen, and what He kept to Himself so that no one was informed of it."

وقيل: ما تُبْصِرُونَ: الإنس وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ: الجن والملائكة. وقال ابن عطا: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار القدرة وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من أسرار القرية.

"It was also said: 'What you see' is mankind, and 'what you do not see' is the jinn and the angels. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: 'What you see' is of the traces of power, and 'what you do not see' is of the secrets of the Unseen."

إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ أي تلاوة محمد وتبليغه، وقيل: لقول مرسل رسول كريم فحذف كقوله وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]] .

"Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger [*qawlu rasūlin karīm*], meaning the recitation and conveyance of Muḥammad. It was also said: it is the word of a sent messenger, with the word omitted, like His saying: 'And ask the town' [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]]."

وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب أبو حاتم: يؤمنون ويذكرون بالياء، وغيرهم بالتاء فيهما تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ تخرّص واختلق عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ قيل: من صلة مجازه:

"'And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.' Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqūb and Abū Ḥātim read *yu'minūna* and *yadhakkarūna* with the yā’, while the others read them with the tā’ in both places. 'It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings [*taqawwala*, meaning he invented and forged], We would have seized him by the right hand.' It was said: this is a metaphor meaning:"

لعاقبناه وانتقمنا منه بالحق كقوله: قالُوا إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]] أي من قبل الحق.

"'We would have punished him and avenged Ourselves upon him with the truth,' like His saying: 'You used to come to us from the right' [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]], meaning from the side of truth."

وقال ابن عباس: لأخذناه بالقوة والقدرة، كقول الشاعر:

إذا ما راية رفعت لمجد ... تلقّاها غرابة باليمن [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

"Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'We would have seized him with strength and power,' like the poet's words:

'When a banner is raised for glory, / Gharābah receives it with the right hand.'" [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

وقيل: معناه لأخذنا منه باليد اليمنى من يديه، وهو مثل معناه لأذللناه وأهناه، وهذا كقوله: ذي السلطان إذا أراد الاستخفاف ببعض من بين يديه، واهانته لبعض أعوانه، خذ بيده فاقمه، واعتمد ابن جرير هذا التأويل.

"It was also said: the meaning is 'We would have seized him by his right hand from his hands,' and this is an image meaning 'We would have humiliated him and disgraced him.' This is like the case of a ruler who wishes to belittle someone before him, or to humiliate one of his aides: he takes his hand and makes him stand. Ibn Jarīr adopted this interpretation."

ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ نياط القلب، عن ابن عباس وأكثر الناس، وقال قتادة: حبل القلب، وقال مجاهد: الحبل الذي في الظهر. وقيل: هو عرق بين العلباء والحلقوم.

"'Then We would have cut from him the *watīn*', the heart's tendon, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and most people. Qatādah said: it is the cord of the heart. Mujāhid said: it is the cord in the back. It was also said: it is a vein between the *ʿalbāʾ* (nape) and the throat."

فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ مانعين يحجزوننا عن عقوبته وما نفعله به وإنّما جمع وهو فعل واحد ردا على معناه كقوله: لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]] ،

"'Then not one of you could withhold Us from him', meaning preventing Us from punishing him and from what We do to him. The plural *ḥājizīn* is used although the verb is singular, returning to the sense of the word *aḥad* (one), like His saying: 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers' [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]],"

وقال (عليه السلام) :

«لم تحل الغنائم لأحد [[في بعض المصادر: لقوم.]] سود الرؤوس [ممّن] قبلكم»

[30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] لفظه واحد ومعناه الجميع.

"and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Spoils were not made lawful for any black-headed one [*li-aḥad* (for anyone)] [*li-qawm* in some sources] before you [*mimman qablakum*].' [30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] Its wording is singular and its meaning is plural."

وَإِنَّهُ يعني القرآن لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ إذا رأوا ثواب متابعيه وقد خالفوه. وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ أضافه إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ الذي كلّ شيء في جنب عظمته صغير.

"'And indeed it, meaning the Qur'an, is a reminder for the God-fearing. And indeed We know that among you are deniers. And indeed it is a cause of anguish for the disbelievers' when they see the reward of its followers while they opposed it. 'And indeed it is the certain truth', which he attributed to Himself because the two wordings differ. 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty', He before whose greatness everything is small."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 69, verses 18–52:**

يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لا تَخْفى بالياء كوفي غير عاصم والباقون بالتاء مِنْكُمْ خافِيَةٌ

"On that Day you will be exposed; not hidden [*la takhfa*, with the yā’ read by Kūfī readers other than ʿĀṣim, and with the tā’ by the rest] from you will be any secret."

In a ḥadīth he said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the first two, they are disputes, quarrels [*ghayr mawjūda fī al-maṣdar*.] and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly into their hands, so one will take his book in his right hand and another will take it in his left." [27] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/414.]]

فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ أي تعالوا اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ ها الوقف وأخواته مثله إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ علمت وأيقنت أَنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ.

"As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: 'Here, take [*hāʾumu*, meaning come here] and read my record [*iqraʾū kitābiyah*]. Indeed, I was certain [*ẓanantu*, meaning I knew and was sure] that I would meet my reckoning.'" The pausal *hāʾ* (*ha al-waqf*) and its like are treated the same way.

Al-Ḥasan informed us, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Qayyim ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Marwazī narrated to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, saying: Marḥūm ibn Abī Arṭabān, the paternal cousin of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAwn, narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of this Ummah to be given his record in his right hand will be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he will have a radiance like the radiance of the sun!" It was said to him: "Then where is Abū Bakr?" He said: "Far, far! The angels have escorted him to Paradise!" [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/269.]]

Al-Ḥasan informed us, narrating to us Manṣūr ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Nahāwandī, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Asʿad al-Burūjirdī narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr narrated to us from Ḥammād, from Salamah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O ʿĀʾishah, all people will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except Abū Bakr." [28] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 11/558, ḥ 32635, and ḥ 32636 with variation.]]

فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ مرضية كقوله: ماءٍ دافِقٍ [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]] وقيل: ذات رضا مثل لأبن وتأمن فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ رفيعة قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ ثمارها قريبة ينالها القائم والقاعد والمضطجع، يقال لهم كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ قدّمتم لآخرتكم من الأعمال الصالحة في الأيام الماضية وهي الدنيا.

"So he will be in a pleasing life [*ʿīshatin rāḍiyah*], meaning one that is pleased, like His saying: [*māʾin dāfiq*, a gushing fluid] [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]]. It was also said: meaning one that has contentment, like *labin* and *tāmin*. In a lofty Garden [*jannatin ʿāliyah*], lofty and elevated, its fruits [*quṭūfuhā*] near at hand, meaning its fruits are close. Those who stand, sit or lie down can reach them. It will be said to them: 'Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past [*al-ayyām al-khāliyah*]', meaning the righteous deeds you sent forward for your Hereafter during the past days, which are the life of this world."

Al-Ḥusayn informed me, saying: al-Quṭayʿī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullāh narrated to us, saying: I was informed from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: I heard Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Khayfī say: "It has reached us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'O My friends, how long I have looked at you in the world, while your lips were dried of drinks, your eyes were sunken, and your bellies were emptied. So be today in your bliss, and eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past.'"

وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ قال ابن الثابت: تلوى يده اليسرى خلف ظهره ثمّ يعطى كتابه. وقيل: تنزع من صدره إلى خلف ظهره فَيَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ وَلَمْ أَدْرِ ما حِسابِيَهْ يا لَيْتَها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ يقول: يا ليت الموتة التي متّها في الدنيا كانت القاضية الفارغة من كل ما بعدها، فلم أبعث بعده، والقاضية موت الأحياء بعدها. وقيل: معناه يا ليتني متّ فاسترحت. قال قتادة: تمنّى الموت ولم يكن عنده في الدنيا شيء أكره من الموت.

"As for him who is given his record in his left hand, Ibn al-Thābit said: His left hand will be twisted behind his back, and then his record will be given to him. It was also said: it will be pulled out from his chest to behind his back. He will say: 'Would that I had not been given my record, and had not known my reckoning! Would that it had been the end [*al-qāḍiyah*]!' He means: Would that the death I died in the world had been the decisive end, with nothing after it, so that I would not have been raised after it. *Al-qāḍiyah* is the death after which there is no living. It was also said: the meaning is 'Would that I had died and been at rest.' Qatādah said: He wished for death, and there was nothing in the world more hateful to him than death."

ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ ذهبت عنّي حجّتي عن أكثر المفسّرين، وقال ابن زيد: زال عنّي ملكي وقولي فيقول الله لخزنة جهنّم: خُذُوهُ، ويروى أنّه يجتمع على شخص واحد من أهل النار مائة ألف من الزبانية، فيقطع في أيديهم قال: فلا يرى على أيديهم منه إلّا الودك، ثمّ يعاد خلقا جديدا.

"My wealth has not availed me; my authority has perished from me [*halaka ʿannī sulṭāniyah*]. According to most of the exegetes, this means my proof has gone from me. Ibn Zayd said: my kingdom and my speech have departed from me. Then Allah will say to the guardians of Hell: 'Seize him!' It is related that a hundred thousand of the Zabaniyah will gather upon one person from the people of the Fire, and they will be cut to pieces in their hands. He said: 'Nothing will be seen on their hands from him except the grease, and then he will be restored to a new creation.'"

فَغُلُّوهُ ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ أدخلوه ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ فأدخلوه في ذراع الملك، فيدخل دبره ويخرج من منخريه. وقيل: يدخل من فيه ويخرج من دبره.

"'Seize him and bind him, then burn him in the Blaze [*ṣallūhu*, meaning cast him in]. Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits [*dhirāʿan*], thread him [*fa-usluku̇hu*]', meaning they will insert him into the cubit of the king, so it enters through his anus and comes out through his nostrils. It was also said: it enters through his mouth and exits through his anus."

روى سفيان عن بسر بن دعلوق عن نوف البكالي قال: كلّ ذراع سبعون باعا والباع أبعد ممّا بينك وبين مكّة، وكان في رحبة الكوفة [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]] .

"Sufyān narrated from Bisr ibn Daʿlūq, from Nawf al-Bakālī, who said: Each cubit is seventy fathoms [*bāʿ*], and the fathom is farther than the distance between you and Makkah. It was in the courtyard [*raḥbah*] of Kufa." [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 29/78.]]

وقال سفيان الثوري: كلّ ذراع من سبعين ذراعا سبعون ذراعا وقال: بأي ذراع هو؟،

"Sufyān al-Thawrī said: Each cubit of the seventy cubits is seventy cubits. And he said: 'By which cubit is it?'"

وقال عبد الله بن عمرو ابن العاص: قال رسول الله ﷺ‎: «لو أن رصاصة مثل هذه- وأشار إلى جمجمة- أرسلت من السماء إلى الأرض فهي مسيرة خمسمائة سنة بلغت الأرض قبل الليل، ولو أنّها أرسلت من رأس السلسلة لسارت أربعين خريفا الليل والنهار قبل أن تبلغ أصلها أو قعرها» [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]] .

"ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If a lead ball like this one—and he pointed to a skull—were sent down from the sky to the earth, it would take five hundred years to reach the earth, and it would arrive before nightfall. But if it were sent from the head of the chain, it would travel forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its base or its bottom.'" [29] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/197.]]

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا ابن حبش قال: حدّثنا ابن زنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن عليّ قال: حدّثنا سلمة قال: حدّثنا عبد الرزاق قال: حدّثنا بكار ابن عبد الله عن ابن أبي مليكة عن عبد الله بن حنظلة عن كعب في قوله: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ قال: لو جمع حديد الدنيا ما وزن حلقة منها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Ḥabash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Bakkār ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to us from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥanẓalah, from Kaʿb, regarding His saying: 'Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him.' He said: 'If all the iron of the world were gathered, it would not weigh one link of it.'"

وأخبرني ابن فنجويه قال: حدّثنا موسى بن محمد قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن علويه قال:

حدّثنا إسماعيل بن عيسى قال: حدّثنا المسيب قال: حدّثنا سويد بن يحيى قال: بلغني أن جميع أهل النار في تلك السلسلة، ولو أن حلقة منها وضعت على جبل لذاب من حرّها.

"Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlawayh narrated to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyib narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: It has reached me that all the people of the Fire are in that chain, and if one link of it were placed on a mountain, it would melt from its heat."

إِنَّهُ كانَ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هاهُنا حَمِيمٌ صديق، وقيل: قريب يعينه، وقيل: هو مأخوذ من الحميم، وهو الماء الحار كأنه الصديق الذي يرق ويحترق قلبه له. وَلا طَعامٌ وليس له اليوم طعام. إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ وهو صديد أهل النار مأخوذ من الغسل كأنه غسالة جروحهم وقروحهم، وقال الضحاك والربيع: هو شجر يأكله أهل النار. لا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخاطِؤُنَ المذنبون وهم الكافرون.

"Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty, and did not urge the feeding of the needy. So today he has no close friend here [*ḥamīm*], meaning a friend. It was also said: a relative who would help him. It was also said: it is derived from *ḥamīm*, which is hot water, as if he were a friend whose heart softens and burns for him. And no food [*ṭaʿām*], meaning he has no food today, except from *ghislīn*, which is the pus of the people of the Fire, derived from *ghasl* (washing), as if it were the washings of their wounds and sores. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Rabīʿ said: it is a tree that the people of the Fire eat. None eat it except *al-khāṭiʾūn*, meaning the sinners, who are the disbelievers."

فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِما تُبْصِرُونَ وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ ترون وما لا ترون، وأراد جميع المكونات والموجودات، وقيل: الدنيا والآخرة. وقيل: ما في ظهر السماء والأرض وما في بطنها. وقيل:

الأجسام والأرواح.

"'So I swear by what you see and what you do not see' [*fa-lā uqsimu*]: what you see and what you do not see. He intended all created things and existing things. It was also said: this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: what is on the surface of the heaven and earth and what is in their depths. It was also said: bodies and spirits."

وقيل: النعم الظاهرة والباطنة.

"It was also said: the apparent and hidden blessings."

وقال جعفر الصادق: بِما تُبْصِرُونَ من صنعي في ملكي وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من برّي بأوليائي.

"Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: 'What you see' is of My making in My kingdom, and 'what you do not see' is of My kindness to My friends."

وقال الجنيد: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار الرسالة والوحي على حسن محمد وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من السر معه ليلة الإسراء. وقيل: ما أظهر الله للملائكة واللوح والقلم، وما استأثر بعلمه فلم يطلع عليه أحدا.

"al-Junayd said: 'What you see' is of the signs of the message and revelation upon the beauty of Muḥammad, and 'what you do not see' is of the secret with him on the night of the Isrāʾ (Night Journey). It was also said: what Allah revealed to the angels, the Preserved Tablet and the Pen, and what He kept to Himself so that no one was informed of it."

وقيل: ما تُبْصِرُونَ: الإنس وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ: الجن والملائكة. وقال ابن عطا: ما تُبْصِرُونَ من آثار القدرة وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ من أسرار القرية.

"It was also said: 'What you see' is mankind, and 'what you do not see' is the jinn and the angels. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: 'What you see' is of the traces of power, and 'what you do not see' is of the secrets of the Unseen."

إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ أي تلاوة محمد وتبليغه، وقيل: لقول مرسل رسول كريم فحذف كقوله وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]] .

"Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger [*qawlu rasūlin karīm*], meaning the recitation and conveyance of Muḥammad. It was also said: it is the word of a sent messenger, with the word omitted, like His saying: 'And ask the town' [[Sūrat Yūsuf: 82.]]."

وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب أبو حاتم: يؤمنون ويذكرون بالياء، وغيرهم بالتاء فيهما تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ تخرّص واختلق عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ قيل: من صلة مجازه:

"'And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.' Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqūb and Abū Ḥātim read *yu'minūna* and *yadhakkarūna* with the yā’, while the others read them with the tā’ in both places. 'It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings [*taqawwala*, meaning he invented and forged], We would have seized him by the right hand.' It was said: this is a metaphor meaning:"

لعاقبناه وانتقمنا منه بالحق كقوله: قالُوا إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]] أي من قبل الحق.

"'We would have punished him and avenged Ourselves upon him with the truth,' like His saying: 'You used to come to us from the right' [[Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 28.]], meaning from the side of truth."

وقال ابن عباس: لأخذناه بالقوة والقدرة، كقول الشاعر:

إذا ما راية رفعت لمجد ... تلقّاها غرابة باليمن [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

"Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'We would have seized him with strength and power,' like the poet's words:

'When a banner is raised for glory, / Gharābah receives it with the right hand.'" [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 1/180.]]

وقيل: معناه لأخذنا منه باليد اليمنى من يديه، وهو مثل معناه لأذللناه وأهناه، وهذا كقوله: ذي السلطان إذا أراد الاستخفاف ببعض من بين يديه، واهانته لبعض أعوانه، خذ بيده فاقمه، واعتمد ابن جرير هذا التأويل.

"It was also said: the meaning is 'We would have seized him by his right hand from his hands,' and this is an image meaning 'We would have humiliated him and disgraced him.' This is like the case of a ruler who wishes to belittle someone before him, or to humiliate one of his aides: he takes his hand and makes him stand. Ibn Jarīr adopted this interpretation."

ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ نياط القلب، عن ابن عباس وأكثر الناس، وقال قتادة: حبل القلب، وقال مجاهد: الحبل الذي في الظهر. وقيل: هو عرق بين العلباء والحلقوم.

"'Then We would have cut from him the *watīn*', the heart's tendon, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and most people. Qatādah said: it is the cord of the heart. Mujāhid said: it is the cord in the back. It was also said: it is a vein between the *ʿalbāʾ* (nape) and the throat."

فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ مانعين يحجزوننا عن عقوبته وما نفعله به وإنّما جمع وهو فعل واحد ردا على معناه كقوله: لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]] ،

"'Then not one of you could withhold Us from him', meaning preventing Us from punishing him and from what We do to him. The plural *ḥājizīn* is used although the verb is singular, returning to the sense of the word *aḥad* (one), like His saying: 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers' [[Sūrat al-Baqarah: 285.]],"

وقال (عليه السلام) :

«لم تحل الغنائم لأحد [[في بعض المصادر: لقوم.]] سود الرؤوس [ممّن] قبلكم»

[30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] لفظه واحد ومعناه الجميع.

"and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Spoils were not made lawful for any black-headed one [*li-aḥad* (for anyone)] [*li-qawm* in some sources] before you [*mimman qablakum*].' [30] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/276, and Aḥkām al-Qurʾān by al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 3/60.]] Its wording is singular and its meaning is plural."

وَإِنَّهُ يعني القرآن لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ إذا رأوا ثواب متابعيه وقد خالفوه. وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ أضافه إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ الذي كلّ شيء في جنب عظمته صغير.

"'And indeed it, meaning the Qur'an, is a reminder for the God-fearing. And indeed We know that among you are deniers. And indeed it is a cause of anguish for the disbelievers' when they see the reward of its followers while they opposed it. 'And indeed it is the certain truth', which he attributed to Himself because the two wordings differ. 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty', He before whose greatness everything is small."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 69, verses 18–52:**

يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لا تَخْفى بالياء كوفي غير عاصم والباقون بالتاء مِنْكُمْ خافِيَةٌ

"On that Day you will be exposed; not hidden [*la takhfa*, with the yā’ read by Kūfī readers other than ʿĀṣim, and with the tā’ by the rest] from you will be any secret."

In a ḥadīth he said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the first two, they are disputes, quarrels [*ghayr mawjūda fī al-maṣdar*.] and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly into their hands, so one will take his book in his right hand and another will take it in his left." [27] [[Musnad Aḥmad: 4/414.]]

فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ أي تعالوا اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ ها الوقف وأخواته مثله إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ علمت وأيقنت أَنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ.

"As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: 'Here, take [*hāʾumu*, meaning come here] and read my record [*iqraʾū kitābiyah*]. Indeed, I was certain [*ẓanantu*, meaning I knew and was sure] that I would meet my reckoning.'" The pausal *hāʾ* (*ha al-waqf*) and its like are treated the same way.

Al-Ḥasan informed us, saying: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Qayyim ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Marwazī narrated to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, saying: Marḥūm ibn Abī Arṭabān, the paternal cousin of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAwn, narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of this Ummah to be given his record in his right hand will be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he will have a radiance like the radiance of the sun!" It was said to him: "Then where is Abū Bakr?" He said: "Far, far! The angels have escorted him to Paradise!" [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/269.]]

Al-Ḥasan informed us, narrating to us Manṣūr ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Nahāwandī, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Asʿad al-Burūjirdī narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr narrated to us from Ḥammād, from Salamah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O ʿĀʾishah, all people will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except Abū Bakr." [28] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 11/558, ḥ 32635, and ḥ 32636 with variation.]]

فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ مرضية كقوله: ماءٍ دافِقٍ [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]] وقيل: ذات رضا مثل لأبن وتأمن فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ رفيعة قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ ثمارها قريبة ينالها القائم والقاعد والمضطجع، يقال لهم كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ قدّمتم لآخرتكم من الأعمال الصالحة في الأيام الماضية وهي الدنيا.

"So he will be in a pleasing life [*ʿīshatin rāḍiyah*], meaning one that is pleased, like His saying: [*māʾin dāfiq*, a gushing fluid] [[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 6.]]. It was also said: meaning one that has contentment, like *labin* and *tāmin*. In a lofty Garden [*jannatin ʿāliyah*], lofty and elevated, its fruits [*quṭūfuhā*] near at hand, meaning its fruits are close. Those who stand, sit or lie down can reach them. It will be said to them: 'Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past [*al-ayyām al-khāliyah*]', meaning the righteous deeds you sent forward for your Hereafter during the past days, which are the life of this world."

Al-Ḥusayn informed me, saying: al-Quṭayʿī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullāh narrated to us, saying: I was informed from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: I heard Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Khayfī say: "It has reached us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'O My friends, how long I have looked at you in the world, while your lips were dried of drinks, your eyes were sunken, and your bellies were emptied. So be today in your bliss, and eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days that are past.'"

وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ قال ابن الثابت: تلوى يده اليسرى خلف ظهره ثمّ يعطى كتابه. وقيل: تنزع من صدره إلى خلف ظهره فَيَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ وَلَمْ أَدْرِ ما حِسابِيَهْ يا لَيْتَها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ يقول: يا ليت الموتة التي متّها في الدنيا كانت القاضية الفارغة من كل ما بعدها، فلم أبعث بعده، والقاضية موت الأحياء بعدها. وقيل: معناه يا ليتني متّ فاسترحت. قال قتادة: تمنّى الموت ولم يكن عنده في الدنيا شيء أكره من الموت.

"As for him who is given his record in his left hand, Ibn al-Thābit said: His left hand will be twisted behind his back, and then his record will be given to him. It was also said: it will be pulled out from his chest to behind his back. He will say: 'Would that I had not been given my record, and had not known my reckoning! Would that it had been the end [*al-qāḍiyah*]!' He means: Would that the death I died in the world had been the decisive end, with nothing after it, so that I would not have been raised after it. *Al-qāḍiyah* is the death after which there is no living.
